`client/src/og_text.c`:

```c
/* Colour nicks and colour items: the 2018 client draws every text with GDI (TextOutW into a DIB that becomes a texture,
 * see docs/04). The server sends name -> colour and item name -> colour lists (OG_S_COLORS); this hook changes the
 * text colour of matching strings. Outlined texts (name balloons) are handled in og_ui.c. */
#include "og.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <wchar.h>
#include "../../third_party/minhook/include/MinHook.h"

#define BUCKETS 1024
#define MAX_TEXT 64

typedef struct entry { struct entry *next; uint8_t kind; COLORREF color; wchar_t text[MAX_TEXT]; } entry;

static entry *g_table[BUCKETS];
static SRWLOCK g_lock = SRWLOCK_INIT;
static volatile LONG g_count;
static int g_textlog;

typedef BOOL (WINAPI *textoutw_t)(HDC, int, int, LPCWSTR, int);
static textoutw_t o_textoutw;

static unsigned hash(const wchar_t *s, size_t n)
{
    unsigned h = 2166136261u;
    size_t i;
    for (i = 0; i < n; i++) { h ^= (unsigned)s[i]; h *= 16777619u; }
    return h & (BUCKETS - 1);
}

static entry *find(const wchar_t *s, size_t n, uint8_t kind)
{
    entry *e;
    if (!n || n >= MAX_TEXT) return NULL;
    for (e = g_table[hash(s, n)]; e; e = e->next)
        if (e->kind == kind && wcsncmp(e->text, s, n) == 0 && e->text[n] == 0) return e;
    return NULL;
}

void og_colors_update(uint8_t kind, uint8_t op, const uint8_t *p, size_t n)
{
    size_t pos = 0;
    int i;
    AcquireSRWLockExclusive(&g_lock);
    if (op == OG_COLOR_OP_REPLACE) {
        for (i = 0; i < BUCKETS; i++) {
            entry **pp = &g_table[i];
            while (*pp) {
                if ((*pp)->kind == kind) { entry *d = *pp; *pp = d->next; free(d); InterlockedDecrement(&g_count); }
                else pp = &(*pp)->next;
            }
        }
    }
    while (pos + 4 <= n) {
        uint8_t len = p[pos + 3];
        wchar_t w[MAX_TEXT];
        int wl;
        COLORREF c = RGB(p[pos], p[pos + 1], p[pos + 2]);
        if (pos + 4 + len > n) break;
        wl = MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP, 0, (const char *)p + pos + 4, len, w, MAX_TEXT - 1);
        pos += 4 + len;
        if (wl <= 0) continue;
        w[wl] = 0;
        {
            entry *e = find(w, wl, kind);
            if (op == OG_COLOR_OP_REMOVE) {
                if (e) {
                    entry **pp = &g_table[hash(w, wl)];
                    while (*pp != e) pp = &(*pp)->next;
                    *pp = e->next;
                    free(e);
                    InterlockedDecrement(&g_count);
                }
            } else if (e) {
                e->color = c;
            } else if ((e = (entry *)calloc(1, sizeof *e)) != NULL) {
                unsigned h = hash(w, wl);
                e->kind = kind;
                e->color = c;
                wcsncpy(e->text, w, MAX_TEXT - 1);
                e->next = g_table[h];
                g_table[h] = e;
                InterlockedIncrement(&g_count);
            }
        }
    }
    ReleaseSRWLockExclusive(&g_lock);
}

static int is_digit(wchar_t c) { return c >= L'0' && c <= L'9'; }

/* "+7 Blade [4]", "Jellopy: 5 ea", "Jellopy 5 ea" -> "Blade", "Jellopy" */
static void item_key(const wchar_t *s, size_t n, size_t *start, size_t *len)
{
    size_t a = 0, b = n;
    if (n > 2 && s[0] == L'+' && is_digit(s[1])) {
        a = 1;
        while (a < n && is_digit(s[a])) a++;
        while (a < n && s[a] == L' ') a++;
    }
    if (b > a + 3 && s[b - 1] == L']') {                 /* " [4]" slots */
        size_t i = b - 2;
        while (i > a && is_digit(s[i])) i--;
        if (s[i] == L'[') { b = i; while (b > a && s[b - 1] == L' ') b--; }
    }
    if (b > a + 3 && s[b - 2] == L'e' && s[b - 1] == L'a') { /* ": 5 ea" / " 5 ea" */
        size_t i = b - 2;
        while (i > a && s[i - 1] == L' ') i--;
        while (i > a && is_digit(s[i - 1])) i--;
        while (i > a && (s[i - 1] == L' ' || s[i - 1] == L':')) i--;
        b = i;
    }
    *start = a;
    *len = b - a;
}

static int lookup(const wchar_t *s, int n, COLORREF *out)
{
    entry *e;
    size_t a, l, k;
    if (n <= 0 || !g_count) return 0;
    /* names: "Name" or "Name (Party)" */
    for (k = 0; k < (size_t)n && !(s[k] == L' ' && k + 1 < (size_t)n && s[k + 1] == L'('); k++) { }
    if ((e = find(s, k, OG_COLOR_NAME)) != NULL) { *out = e->color; return 1; }
    item_key(s, n, &a, &l);
    if ((e = find(s + a, l, OG_COLOR_ITEM)) != NULL) { *out = e->color; return 1; }
    return 0;
}

/* set while UIWindow::TextOutWithOutline runs: that function already got the right colour, its outline passes
   must stay black */
static DWORD g_tls_in_outline = TLS_OUT_OF_INDEXES;

int og_colors_lookup_a(const char *text, int len, COLORREF *out)
{
    wchar_t w[MAX_TEXT];
    int wl, hit;
    if (!g_count || !text) return 0;
    if (len <= 0) len = (int)strlen(text);
    wl = MultiByteToWideChar(CP_ACP, 0, text, len < MAX_TEXT - 1 ? len : MAX_TEXT - 1, w, MAX_TEXT - 1);
    if (wl <= 0) return 0;
    AcquireSRWLockShared(&g_lock);
    hit = lookup(w, wl, out);
    ReleaseSRWLockShared(&g_lock);
    return hit;
}

void og_text_outline_scope(int enter)
{
    if (g_tls_in_outline != TLS_OUT_OF_INDEXES) TlsSetValue(g_tls_in_outline, (LPVOID)(INT_PTR)enter);
}

static BOOL WINAPI h_textoutw(HDC dc, int x, int y, LPCWSTR s, int n)
{
    COLORREF want, cur;
    BOOL r;
    int hit;
    if (g_textlog && s && n > 0 && n < 80) og_log("text %06lx '%.*ls'", (unsigned long)GetTextColor(dc), n, s);
    if (!s || n <= 0 || !g_count) return o_textoutw(dc, x, y, s, n);
    if (g_tls_in_outline != TLS_OUT_OF_INDEXES && TlsGetValue(g_tls_in_outline)) return o_textoutw(dc, x, y, s, n);
    AcquireSRWLockShared(&g_lock);
    hit = lookup(s, n, &want);
    ReleaseSRWLockShared(&g_lock);
    if (!hit) return o_textoutw(dc, x, y, s, n);
    cur = GetTextColor(dc);
    /* outline and shadow passes are drawn in black/very dark colours first; keep them */
    if (g_textlog) og_log("colour hit '%.*ls' cur %06lx want %06lx", n, s, (unsigned long)cur, (unsigned long)want);
    SetTextColor(dc, want);
    r = o_textoutw(dc, x, y, s, n);
    SetTextColor(dc, cur);
    return r;
}

int og_text_init(void)
{
    char p[MAX_PATH];
    void *target = (void *)GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleA("gdi32.dll") ? GetModuleHandleA("gdi32.dll") : LoadLibraryA("gdi32.dll"), "TextOutW");
    g_tls_in_outline = TlsAlloc();
    snprintf(p, sizeof p, "%s\\odinguard.ini", og_client_dir);
    g_textlog = GetPrivateProfileIntA("OdinGuard", "TextLog", 0, p);
    if (!target || MH_CreateHook(target, (void *)h_textoutw, (void **)&o_textoutw) != MH_OK) return 0;
    return MH_EnableHook(target) == MH_OK;
}
```

`client/src/og_ui.c`:

```c
/* Hooks inside the game exe. Every hook is bound to a byte signature of the target function; when the exe is a
 * different build the signature does not match and the hook is skipped (logged), so OdinGuard never patches
 * unknown code.
 *
 * UIWindow::TextOutWithOutline (2018-06-20: 0x006fd780, thiscall, ret 0x24):
 *   (x, y, text, len, fg colour, outline colour, font type, font height, bold)
 * draws the outline in four passes and then the text. The name balloons over characters use it, so colour nicks
 * replace the fg colour here. */
#include "og.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "../../third_party/minhook/include/MinHook.h"

void og_text_outline_scope(int enter);
int og_colors_lookup_a(const char *text, int len, COLORREF *out);

typedef void (__fastcall *textoutline_t)(void *self, void *edx, int x, int y, const char *text, int len,
                                         COLORREF fg, COLORREF outline, int font, int height, int bold);
static textoutline_t o_textoutline;

static void __fastcall h_textoutline(void *self, void *edx, int x, int y, const char *text, int len,
                                     COLORREF fg, COLORREF outline, int font, int height, int bold)
{
    COLORREF want;
    if (text && og_colors_lookup_a(text, len, &want)) fg = want;
    og_text_outline_scope(1);
    o_textoutline(self, edx, x, y, text, len, fg, outline, font, height, bold);
    og_text_outline_scope(0);
}

typedef struct { const char *name; uintptr_t rva; const uint8_t *sig; size_t siglen; void *detour; void **orig; } og_patch;

static const uint8_t sig_textoutline[] = { 0x55, 0x8B, 0xEC, 0x6A, 0xFF, 0x68, 0x98, 0x92, 0xB8, 0x00, 0x64, 0xA1, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00, 0x00,
                                           0x50, 0x83, 0xEC, 0x24, 0x53, 0x56, 0x57 };

/* alpha.exe is packed: its code is written after the DLLs are loaded, so the hooks wait until the
   signatures appear (checked every 100 ms for up to 60 s) */
static DWORD WINAPI ui_thread(LPVOID p)
{
    og_patch patches[] = {
        { "TextOutWithOutline", 0x006fd780 - 0x400000, sig_textoutline, sizeof sig_textoutline, (void *)h_textoutline, (void **)&o_textoutline },
    };
    uint8_t *base = (uint8_t *)GetModuleHandleA(NULL);
    size_t i;
    int ok = 0, waited;
    (void)p;
    for (i = 0; i < sizeof patches / sizeof *patches; i++) {
        uint8_t *target = base + patches[i].rva;
        int found = 0;
        for (waited = 0; waited < 600 && !found; waited++) {
            MEMORY_BASIC_INFORMATION mbi;
            if (VirtualQuery(target, &mbi, sizeof mbi) && mbi.State == MEM_COMMIT &&
                !(mbi.Protect & (PAGE_NOACCESS | PAGE_GUARD)) && memcmp(target, patches[i].sig, patches[i].siglen) == 0)
                found = 1;
            else
                Sleep(100);
        }
        if (!found) {
            og_log("ui hook %s: signature not found (different client build), skipped", patches[i].name);
            continue;
        }
        if (MH_CreateHook(target, patches[i].detour, patches[i].orig) != MH_OK || MH_EnableHook(target) != MH_OK) {
            og_log("ui hook %s: failed", patches[i].name);
            continue;
        }
        ok++;
    }
    og_log("ui hooks: %d of %d active", ok, (int)(sizeof patches / sizeof *patches));
    return 0;
}

void og_ui_init(void)
{
    CloseHandle(CreateThread(NULL, 0, ui_thread, NULL, 0, NULL));
}

#ifdef OG_TEST_CURSOR
/* test builds only: the Parallels VM forces the guest cursor to the host mouse, so automated tests put the game
   cursor where odinguard.ini [Test] Cursor=x,y (client coordinates, re-read every second) says */
typedef BOOL (WINAPI *getcursorpos_t)(LPPOINT);
static getcursorpos_t o_getcursorpos;
static volatile LONG g_cx = -1, g_cy = -1;

static BOOL WINAPI h_getcursorpos(LPPOINT p)
{
    BOOL r = o_getcursorpos(p);
    if (r && g_cx >= 0) {
        POINT c = { g_cx, g_cy };
        HWND w = FindWindowA(NULL, "Alpha - 20180620");
        if (w && ClientToScreen(w, &c)) *p = c;
    }
    return r;
}

static DWORD WINAPI cursor_thread(LPVOID unused)
{
    char ini[MAX_PATH], v[64];
    (void)unused;
    snprintf(ini, sizeof ini, "%s\\odinguard.ini", og_client_dir);
    for (;;) {
        int x = -1, y = -1;
        GetPrivateProfileStringA("Test", "Cursor", "", v, sizeof v, ini);
        if (sscanf(v, "%d,%d", &x, &y) != 2) x = y = -1;
        InterlockedExchange(&g_cx, x);
        InterlockedExchange(&g_cy, y);
        {
            int k;
            for (k = 0; k < 5; k++) {
                HWND w = FindWindowA(NULL, "Alpha - 20180620");
                if (w && x >= 0) PostMessageA(w, WM_MOUSEMOVE, 0, MAKELPARAM(x, y));
                Sleep(100);
            }
        }
    }
    return 0;
}

void og_test_cursor_init(void)
{
    void *t = (void *)GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleA("user32.dll"), "GetCursorPos");
    if (t && MH_CreateHook(t, (void *)h_getcursorpos, (void **)&o_getcursorpos) == MH_OK && MH_EnableHook(t) == MH_OK) {
        CloseHandle(CreateThread(NULL, 0, cursor_thread, NULL, 0, NULL));
        og_log("TEST BUILD: cursor override active");
    }
}
#endif
```

`client/tests/dettest.c`:

```c
/* Detection test for the cheat-signatures module (og_detect.c linked directly, no network).
 *
 *   dettest <odinguard.sigpack> positive <empty work folder>
 *       For the first signature of every client-checkable kind in the package a harmless stub is created
 *       (renamed copy of ping.exe / version.dll, own window class or title, empty file) and must be reported.
 *       File, GRF and allowlist matching use synthetic hashes of fixture files. No cheat software is involved.
 *   dettest <odinguard.sigpack> clean <client folder>
 *       Every 32-bit DLL of the client folder is mapped (without running its code) and the folder is scanned
 *       like the guard does; any signature hit is a false alarm.
 *
 * Prints PASS/FAIL lines; the exit code is the number of failures. */
#include "og.h"
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

char og_client_dir[MAX_PATH];

#define MAX_HITS 256
static struct { uint16_t id; uint8_t kind; char text[260]; } g_hits[MAX_HITS];
static int g_nhits, g_fail;

void og_net_broadcast_control(const uint8_t *m, size_t n)
{
    if (n < 4 || m[0] != OG_C_DETECT || g_nhits >= MAX_HITS) return;
    g_hits[g_nhits].id = (uint16_t)(m[1] | (m[2] << 8));
    g_hits[g_nhits].kind = m[3];
    snprintf(g_hits[g_nhits].text, sizeof g_hits[0].text, "%.*s", (int)(n - 4), (const char *)m + 4);
    g_nhits++;
}

static void result(int ok, const char *what, const char *detail)
{
    printf("%s %s%s%s\n", ok ? "PASS" : "FAIL", what, detail ? ": " : "", detail ? detail : "");
    if (!ok) g_fail++;
}

static int hit(uint16_t id, uint8_t kind)
{
    int i;
    for (i = 0; i < g_nhits; i++) if (g_hits[i].id == id && g_hits[i].kind == kind) return 1;
    return 0;
}

/* signature package (OGSP v1): entries are taken as they are; the server checks the signature */
static int load_pack(const char *path)
{
    static uint8_t buf[1 << 20];
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "rb");
    size_t len, off = 15;
    unsigned n, i;
    if (!f) return 0;
    len = fread(buf, 1, sizeof buf, f);
    fclose(f);
    if (len < 15 + 64 || memcmp(buf, "OGSP", 4) || buf[4] != 1) return 0;
    n = buf[13] | (buf[14] << 8);
    og_policy.nsig = 0;
    for (i = 0; i < n && off + 6 <= len - 64; i++) {
        uint16_t id = (uint16_t)(buf[off] | (buf[off + 1] << 8));
        uint8_t kind = buf[off + 2], nlen = buf[off + 5], plen;
        off += 6 + nlen;
        plen = buf[off++];
        if (off + plen > len - 64) return 0;
        if (og_policy.nsig < OG_MAX_SIGS) {
            og_signature *s = &og_policy.sig[og_policy.nsig++];
            s->id = id;
            s->kind = kind;
            memcpy(s->pattern, buf + off, plen);
            s->pattern[plen] = 0;
        }
        off += plen;
    }
    return og_policy.nsig;
}

static og_signature *first_of(uint8_t kind)
{
    int i;
    for (i = 0; i < og_policy.nsig; i++) if (og_policy.sig[i].kind == kind) return &og_policy.sig[i];
    return NULL;
}

static void add_sig(uint16_t id, uint8_t kind, const char *pattern)
{
    og_signature *s = &og_policy.sig[og_policy.nsig++];
    s->id = id;
    s->kind = kind;
    snprintf(s->pattern, sizeof s->pattern, "%s", pattern);
}

static void write_file(const char *path, const char *text)
{
    FILE *f = fopen(path, "wb");
    if (f) { fputs(text, f); fclose(f); }
}

static void scan(void)
{
    g_nhits = 0;
    og_detect_reset();
    og_detect_scan();
}

static LRESULT CALLBACK wndproc(HWND w, UINT m, WPARAM wp, LPARAM lp) { return DefWindowProcA(w, m, wp, lp); }

static HWND stub_window(const char *cls, const char *title)
{
    WNDCLASSA wc;
    ZeroMemory(&wc, sizeof wc);
    wc.lpfnWndProc = wndproc;
    wc.hInstance = GetModuleHandleA(NULL);
    wc.lpszClassName = cls;
    RegisterClassA(&wc);
    return CreateWindowA(cls, title, WS_POPUP | WS_VISIBLE, -2000, -2000, 10, 10, NULL, NULL, wc.hInstance, NULL);
}

static int positive(const char *dir)
{
    char sys[MAX_PATH], src[MAX_PATH], dst[MAX_PATH], hex[65], ini[MAX_PATH];
    og_signature *s;
    PROCESS_INFORMATION pi = { 0 };
    HWND w1 = NULL, w2 = NULL;
    HMODULE mod = NULL;
    HANDLE mtx = NULL;
    uint16_t pid_sig = 0, mod_sig = 0, cls_sig = 0, title_sig = 0, file_sig = 0;

    snprintf(og_client_dir, sizeof og_client_dir, "%s", dir);
    GetSystemWow64DirectoryA(sys, sizeof sys);
    if (!sys[0]) GetSystemDirectoryA(sys, sizeof sys);

    if ((s = first_of(OG_KIND_PROCESS))) {
        STARTUPINFOA si;
        char cmd[MAX_PATH * 2];
        ZeroMemory(&si, sizeof si);
        si.cb = sizeof si;
        pid_sig = s->id;
        snprintf(src, sizeof src, "%s\\PING.EXE", sys);
        snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s\\%s%s", dir, s->pattern, og_contains_i(s->pattern, ".exe") ? "" : ".exe");
        CopyFileA(src, dst, FALSE);
        snprintf(cmd, sizeof cmd, "\"%s\" -n 30 127.0.0.1", dst);
        if (!CreateProcessA(dst, cmd, NULL, NULL, FALSE, CREATE_SUSPENDED | CREATE_NO_WINDOW, NULL, NULL, &si, &pi)) pid_sig = 0;
    }
    if ((s = first_of(OG_KIND_MODULE))) {
        mod_sig = s->id;
        snprintf(src, sizeof src, "%s\\version.dll", sys);
        snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s\\%s", dir, s->pattern);
        CopyFileA(src, dst, FALSE);
        if (!(mod = LoadLibraryExA(dst, NULL, DONT_RESOLVE_DLL_REFERENCES))) mod_sig = 0;
    }
    if ((s = first_of(OG_KIND_WINDOW_CLASS))) { cls_sig = s->id; w1 = stub_window(s->pattern, "stub"); }
    if ((s = first_of(OG_KIND_WINDOW))) {
        char title[300];
        title_sig = s->id;
        snprintf(title, sizeof title, "stub%s1", s->pattern);
        w2 = stub_window("OgDetTestTitle", title);
    }
    if ((s = first_of(OG_KIND_FILE_NAME))) {
        file_sig = s->id;
        snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s\\%s", dir, s->pattern);
        write_file(dst, "stub");
    }
    /* synthetic hash signatures over fixture files */
    snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s\\fixture.bin", dir);
    write_file(dst, "OdinGuard detection fixture");
    og_sha256_file(dst, hex);
    add_sig(65001, OG_KIND_FILE_SHA256, hex);
    snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s\\fixture.grf", dir);
    write_file(dst, "Master of Magic fixture grf");
    og_sha256_file(dst, hex);
    add_sig(65002, OG_KIND_GRF_SHA256, hex);
    snprintf(ini, sizeof ini, "%s\\DATA.INI", dir);
    write_file(ini, "[Data]\r\n0=fixture.grf\r\n1=data.grf\r\n");

    /* kernel object, registry key and driver: synthetic signatures over harmless objects */
    {
        static char drv[256];
        SC_HANDLE scm = OpenSCManagerA(NULL, NULL, SC_MANAGER_ENUMERATE_SERVICE);
        HKEY k;
        mtx = CreateMutexA(NULL, FALSE, "OdinGuardDetTestMutex");
        add_sig(65005, OG_KIND_MUTEX, "OdinGuardDetTestMutex");
        if (RegCreateKeyExA(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, "Software\\OdinGuardDetTest", 0, NULL, 0, KEY_WRITE, NULL, &k, NULL) == ERROR_SUCCESS) RegCloseKey(k);
        add_sig(65006, OG_KIND_REGISTRY, "HKCU\\Software\\OdinGuardDetTest");
        add_sig(65008, OG_KIND_REGISTRY, "HKCU\\Software\\OdinGuardDetTestMissing");
        if (scm) {
            DWORD need = 0, count = 0, resume = 0;
            ENUM_SERVICE_STATUSA *buf;
            EnumServicesStatusA(scm, SERVICE_DRIVER, SERVICE_ACTIVE, NULL, 0, &need, &count, &resume);
            if (need && (buf = (ENUM_SERVICE_STATUSA *)HeapAlloc(GetProcessHeap(), 0, need))) {
                resume = 0;
                if (EnumServicesStatusA(scm, SERVICE_DRIVER, SERVICE_ACTIVE, buf, need, &need, &count, &resume) && count)
                    snprintf(drv, sizeof drv, "%s", buf[0].lpServiceName);
                HeapFree(GetProcessHeap(), 0, buf);
            }
            CloseServiceHandle(scm);
        }
        if (drv[0]) add_sig(65007, OG_KIND_DRIVER, drv);
        printf("  driver used for the driver test: %s\n", drv[0] ? drv : "(none)");
    }

    scan();
    {
        int i;
        for (i = 0; i < g_nhits; i++) printf("  hit kind %u id %u: %s\n", g_hits[i].kind, g_hits[i].id, g_hits[i].text);
    }
    if (pid_sig) result(hit(pid_sig, OG_KIND_PROCESS), "process name signature", NULL);
    if (mod_sig) result(hit(mod_sig, OG_KIND_MODULE), "loaded module signature", NULL);
    if (cls_sig) result(hit(cls_sig, OG_KIND_WINDOW_CLASS), "window class signature", NULL);
    if (title_sig) result(hit(title_sig, OG_KIND_WINDOW), "window title signature", NULL);
    if (file_sig) result(hit(file_sig, OG_KIND_FILE_NAME), "file name signature", NULL);
    result(hit(65001, OG_KIND_FILE_SHA256), "file hash signature", NULL);
    result(hit(65002, OG_KIND_GRF_SHA256), "GRF hash signature (DATA.INI)", NULL);
    result(hit(65005, OG_KIND_MUTEX), "named mutex signature", NULL);
    result(hit(65006, OG_KIND_REGISTRY), "registry key signature", NULL);
    result(!hit(65008, OG_KIND_REGISTRY), "missing registry key is not reported", NULL);
    result(hit(65007, OG_KIND_DRIVER), "driver / service signature", NULL);
    result(!pid_sig + !mod_sig + !cls_sig + !title_sig + !file_sig == 0, "package has a signature of every stub kind", NULL);

    /* every hit is reported once per connection */
    g_nhits = 0;
    og_detect_scan();
    {
        int i, again = 0;
        for (i = 0; i < g_nhits; i++) if (g_hits[i].id) again++;
        result(again == 0, "hits are not repeated within a connection", NULL);
    }

    /* allowlist: the same files with allowlisted hashes are not reported */
    if (file_sig) {
        snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s\\%s", dir, first_of(OG_KIND_FILE_NAME)->pattern);
        og_sha256_file(dst, hex);
        add_sig(65003, OG_KIND_ALLOW_SHA256, hex);
    }
    snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s\\fixture.bin", dir);
    og_sha256_file(dst, hex);
    add_sig(65004, OG_KIND_ALLOW_SHA256, hex);
    scan();
    result(!hit(65001, OG_KIND_FILE_SHA256), "allowlisted file hash is not reported", NULL);
    if (file_sig) result(!hit(file_sig, OG_KIND_FILE_NAME), "allowlisted file with a signature name is not reported", NULL);

    if (pi.hProcess) { TerminateProcess(pi.hProcess, 0); CloseHandle(pi.hThread); CloseHandle(pi.hProcess); }
    if (mod) FreeLibrary(mod);
    if (w1) DestroyWindow(w1);
    if (w2) DestroyWindow(w2);
    if (mtx) CloseHandle(mtx);
    RegDeleteKeyA(HKEY_CURRENT_USER, "Software\\OdinGuardDetTest");
    return g_fail;
}

static int clean(const char *dir)
{
    char mask[MAX_PATH], full[MAX_PATH];
    WIN32_FIND_DATAA fd;
    HANDLE h;
    int i, mapped = 0, sig_hits = 0;
    snprintf(og_client_dir, sizeof og_client_dir, "%s", dir);
    snprintf(mask, sizeof mask, "%s\\*.dll", dir);
    if ((h = FindFirstFileA(mask, &fd)) != INVALID_HANDLE_VALUE) {
        do {
            snprintf(full, sizeof full, "%s\\%s", dir, fd.cFileName);
            if (LoadLibraryExA(full, NULL, DONT_RESOLVE_DLL_REFERENCES)) { printf("  mapped %s\n", fd.cFileName); mapped++; }
        } while (FindNextFileA(h, &fd));
        FindClose(h);
    }
    scan();
    for (i = 0; i < g_nhits; i++) {
        printf("  %s kind %u id %u: %s\n", g_hits[i].id ? "HIT" : "inject-report", g_hits[i].kind, g_hits[i].id, g_hits[i].text);
        if (g_hits[i].id) sig_hits++;
    }
    result(mapped > 0, "client DLLs mapped", NULL);
    result(sig_hits == 0, "legitimate client folder: no signature hit", NULL);
    return g_fail;
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    InitializeCriticalSection(&og_policy_lock);
    if (argc < 4 || !load_pack(argv[1])) {
        fprintf(stderr, "usage: dettest <odinguard.sigpack> positive|clean <folder>\n");
        return 100;
    }
    printf("%d entries loaded\n", og_policy.nsig);
    if (!strcmp(argv[2], "positive")) return positive(argv[3]);
    if (!strcmp(argv[2], "clean")) return clean(argv[3]);
    return 100;
}
```

`client/tests/fuzz_wire.c`:

```c
/* Native fuzz test of the wire parsers and the PE canonicaliser (proto/og_wire.c), built with ASan + UBSan:
 *   cc -O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -o fuzz_wire tests/fuzz_wire.c ../proto/og_wire.c
 *   ./fuzz_wire [iterations] [seed]
 * Mutates valid seed messages (bit flips, truncation, length fields, random bytes) and checks invariants:
 * no out-of-bounds access (sanitizers), parsers never report more bytes than given, every delivered entry lies
 * inside the buffer, writer output parses back to the same values. */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

#include "../../proto/og_wire.h"

static uint64_t g_rng = 88172645463325252ull;
static uint32_t rnd(void) { g_rng ^= g_rng << 13; g_rng ^= g_rng >> 7; g_rng ^= g_rng << 17; return (uint32_t)g_rng; }

static const uint8_t *g_buf;
static size_t g_len;
static unsigned long g_entries;

#define CHECK(c) do { if (!(c)) { fprintf(stderr, "invariant failed: %s (line %d)\n", #c, __LINE__); abort(); } } while (0)

static void on_sig(void *ctx, uint16_t id, uint8_t kind, const char *p, size_t n)
{
	(void)ctx; (void)id; (void)kind;
	CHECK((const uint8_t *)p >= g_buf && (const uint8_t *)p + n <= g_buf + g_len);
	if (n) { volatile char c = p[n - 1]; (void)c; }
	g_entries++;
}

static void on_color(void *ctx, uint32_t rgb, const char *p, size_t n)
{
	(void)ctx;
	CHECK(rgb <= 0xFFFFFF);
	on_sig(NULL, 0, 0, p, n);
}

static size_t seed_client_hello(uint8_t *b)
{
	size_t n = OG_CLIENT_HELLO_FIXED + 3 * (OG_COMPONENT_NAME + 32), i;
	for (i = 0; i < n; i++) b[i] = (uint8_t)rnd();
	og_wr16(b, OG_HELLO_ID);
	og_wr16(b + 2, (uint16_t)n);
	b[OG_CLIENT_HELLO_FIXED - 1] = 3;
	return n;
}

static size_t seed_sigs(uint8_t *b, uint8_t type)
{
	size_t pos = type == OG_S_SIGS ? 4 : 5, i;
	int k;
	b[0] = type;
	b[1] = 1; b[2] = 1;
	for (k = 0; k < 5; k++) {
		uint8_t len = (uint8_t)(rnd() % 40);
		b[pos] = (uint8_t)k; b[pos + 1] = 0; b[pos + 2] = 3; b[pos + 3] = len;
		for (i = 0; i < len; i++) b[pos + 4 + i] = (uint8_t)('a' + rnd() % 26);
		pos += 4 + len;
	}
	if (type == OG_S_SIGS) og_wr16(b + 2, 5); else og_wr16(b + 3, 5);
	return pos;
}

/* a tiny but valid PE32 with one code section and a relocation block */
static size_t seed_pe(uint8_t *b)
{
	size_t n = 0x600;
	uint32_t lf = 0x80, opt = lf + 24;
	memset(b, 0, n);
	b[0] = 'M'; b[1] = 'Z';
	og_wr32(b + 0x3c, lf);
	memcpy(b + lf, "PE\0\0", 4);
	og_wr16(b + lf + 6, 2);
	og_wr16(b + lf + 20, 224);
	og_wr16(b + opt, 0x10b);
	og_wr32(b + opt + 96 + 5 * 8, 0x2000);   /* reloc rva */
	og_wr32(b + opt + 96 + 5 * 8 + 4, 12);
	/* .text */
	memcpy(b + opt + 224, ".text", 5);
	og_wr32(b + opt + 224 + 8, 0x100); og_wr32(b + opt + 224 + 12, 0x1000);
	og_wr32(b + opt + 224 + 16, 0x200); og_wr32(b + opt + 224 + 20, 0x200);
	og_wr32(b + opt + 224 + 36, 0x60000020);
	/* .reloc */
	memcpy(b + opt + 264, ".reloc", 6);
	og_wr32(b + opt + 264 + 8, 0x20); og_wr32(b + opt + 264 + 12, 0x2000);
	og_wr32(b + opt + 264 + 16, 0x200); og_wr32(b + opt + 264 + 20, 0x400);
	og_wr32(b + opt + 264 + 36, 0x42000040);
	memset(b + 0x200, 0xAB, 0x100);
	og_wr32(b + 0x400, 0x1000); og_wr32(b + 0x404, 12); og_wr16(b + 0x408, 0x3010); og_wr16(b + 0x40a, 0);
	return n;
}

static void mutate(uint8_t *b, size_t *n, size_t cap)
{
	int k, rounds = 1 + rnd() % 4;
	for (k = 0; k < rounds; k++) {
		switch (rnd() % 6) {
		case 0: if (*n) b[rnd() % *n] ^= (uint8_t)(1 << (rnd() % 8)); break;
		case 1: if (*n) *n = rnd() % *n; break;
		case 2: if (*n >= 4) og_wr16(b + 2 + (rnd() % 2), (uint16_t)rnd()); break;
		case 3: if (*n) b[rnd() % *n] = (uint8_t)rnd(); break;
		case 4: { size_t add = rnd() % 64; while (add-- && *n < cap) b[(*n)++] = (uint8_t)rnd(); break; }
		case 5: if (*n > 8) og_wr32(b + rnd() % (*n - 4), rnd()); break;
		}
	}
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
	unsigned long iters = argc > 1 ? strtoul(argv[1], NULL, 10) : 200000, i;
	enum { CAP = 4096 };
	uint8_t *b = (uint8_t *)malloc(CAP);
	if (argc > 2) g_rng = strtoull(argv[2], NULL, 10) | 1;
	for (i = 0; i < iters; i++) {
		size_t n = 0;
		int which = (int)(rnd() % 9), r;
		switch (which) {
		case 0: n = seed_client_hello(b); break;
		case 1: n = OG_SERVER_HELLO_FIXED + 20; memset(b, 0x41, n); og_wr16(b, OG_HELLO_ID); og_wr16(b + 2, (uint16_t)n); break;
		case 2: n = seed_sigs(b, OG_S_SIGS); break;
		case 3: n = seed_sigs(b, OG_S_COLORS); break;
		case 4: n = OG_CHALLENGE_LEN; memset(b, 7, n); b[0] = OG_S_CHALLENGE; break;
		case 5: n = OG_RESPONSE_LEN; memset(b, 9, n); b[0] = OG_C_RESPONSE; break;
		case 6: n = OG_ALIVE_LEN; memset(b, 3, n); b[0] = OG_C_ALIVE; break;
		case 7: n = 18 + 100; memset(b, 0, n); og_wr16(b, 100); break;
		case 8: n = seed_pe(b); break;
		}
		if (rnd() % 8) mutate(b, &n, CAP);
		/* exact-size heap copy so ASan sees every overread */
		{
			uint8_t *m = (uint8_t *)malloc(n ? n : 1);
			memcpy(m, b, n);
			g_buf = m; g_len = n;
			switch (which) {
			case 0: { og_client_hello h; r = og_wire_client_hello(m, n, &h); CHECK(r <= (int)n); if (r > 0) CHECK(h.comp + h.ncomp * 48 <= m + n); break; }
			case 1: { og_server_hello h; r = og_wire_server_hello(m, n, &h); CHECK(r <= (int)n); if (r > 0) CHECK(h.message + h.message_len <= m + n); break; }
			case 2: { uint8_t op; og_wire_sigs(m, n, &op, on_sig, NULL); break; }
			case 3: { uint8_t k, op; og_wire_colors(m, n, &k, &op, on_color, NULL); break; }
			case 4: { og_challenge_msg c; uint8_t out[OG_CHALLENGE_LEN]; og_challenge_msg c2;
				if (og_wire_challenge(m, n, &c) > 0) { og_wire_write_challenge(out, &c); CHECK(og_wire_challenge(out, sizeof out, &c2) > 0 && c2.id == c.id && c2.a == c.a && c2.b == c.b && c2.target == c.target); } break; }
			case 5: { og_response_msg x; uint8_t out[OG_RESPONSE_LEN]; og_response_msg y;
				if (og_wire_response(m, n, &x) > 0) { og_wire_write_response(out, &x); CHECK(og_wire_response(out, sizeof out, &y) > 0 && y.id == x.id && y.status == x.status && !memcmp(y.digest, x.digest, 32)); } break; }
			case 6: { og_alive_msg a; og_wire_alive(m, n, &a); break; }
			case 7: { uint16_t bl = 0; r = og_wire_record(m, n, &bl); if (r > 0) CHECK((size_t)18 + bl <= n); break; }
			case 8: { uint8_t *img = NULL; size_t sz = og_pe_canonical(m, n, OG_CANON_CODE | OG_CANON_RDATA, &img);
				if (sz) { volatile uint8_t x = img[sz - 1]; (void)x; } free(img); break; }
			}
			free(m);
		}
	}
	/* the unmutated PE seed must give the code section with the relocated slot zeroed */
	{
		uint8_t *img = NULL;
		size_t n = seed_pe(b), sz = og_pe_canonical(b, n, OG_CANON_CODE, &img);
		CHECK(sz == 0x100 && img[0x0f] == 0xAB && img[0x10] == 0 && img[0x13] == 0 && img[0x14] == 0xAB);
		free(img);
	}
	printf("fuzz_wire: %lu iterations ok, %lu list entries checked\n", iters, g_entries);
	free(b);
	return 0;
}
```

```c
/* Test helper: brings the RO window to the front and types a line with SendInput (synthetic input).
 *   inject.exe "<text>"  -> result written to inject.out next to the exe */
#include <windows.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <string.h>

static UINT g_ok, g_fail;
static DWORD g_err;

static void key(WORD vk, int up)
{
    INPUT in;
    memset(&in, 0, sizeof in);
    in.type = INPUT_KEYBOARD;
    in.ki.wVk = vk;
    in.ki.dwFlags = up ? KEYEVENTF_KEYUP : 0;
    if (SendInput(1, &in, sizeof in) == 1) g_ok++; else { g_fail++; g_err = GetLastError(); }
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    char out[MAX_PATH], *s;
    FILE *f;
    HWND w = FindWindowA(NULL, "Alpha - 20180620");
    int sent = 0;
    const char *t = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "+heal";
    GetModuleFileNameA(NULL, out, sizeof out);
    s = strrchr(out, '\\');
    strcpy(s + 1, "inject.out");
    if (w) { SetForegroundWindow(w); Sleep(300); }
    for (; *t; t++) {
        SHORT v = VkKeyScanA(*t);
        if (v == -1) continue;
        if (v & 0x100) key(VK_SHIFT, 0);
        key(LOBYTE(v), 0); key(LOBYTE(v), 1);
        if (v & 0x100) key(VK_SHIFT, 1);
        sent++;
        Sleep(40);
    }
    key(VK_RETURN, 0); key(VK_RETURN, 1);
    f = fopen(out, "w");
    if (f) { fprintf(f, "window %p foreground %d sent %d ok %u fail %u err %lu\n", (void *)w, GetForegroundWindow() == w, sent, g_ok, g_fail, g_err); fclose(f); }
    return 0;
}
```

`client/tests/nettest.c`:

```c
/* End-to-end test of the network layer: loads odinguard.dll (hooks ws2_32), then talks plain RO packets.
 *   nettest <ip> <login-port> <user> <password> [char-port]
 * The DLL encrypts everything transparently; the test only sees normal game packets. */
#include <winsock2.h>
#include <windows.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

static ULONGLONG wall_ms(void)
{
    FILETIME f;
    GetSystemTimeAsFileTime(&f);
    return (((ULONGLONG)f.dwHighDateTime << 32) | f.dwLowDateTime) / 10000;
}

static int recv_some(SOCKET s, unsigned char *buf, int cap, int ms)
{
    DWORD end = GetTickCount() + ms;
    int got = 0;
    while ((LONG)(end - GetTickCount()) > 0) {
        fd_set rd;
        struct timeval tv = { 0, 50000 };
        int r;
        FD_ZERO(&rd);
        FD_SET(s, &rd);
        if (select(0, &rd, NULL, NULL, &tv) <= 0) { if (got) break; continue; }
        r = recv(s, (char *)buf + got, cap - got, 0);
        if (r > 0) { got += r; continue; }
        if (r == 0) break;
        if (WSAGetLastError() != WSAEWOULDBLOCK) break;
    }
    return got;
}

/* prints every chat/system message (0x008E) in buf */
static void print_messages(const char *what, const unsigned char *buf, int n)
{
    int k, any = 0;
    for (k = 0; k + 4 < n; k++) {
        if (buf[k] == 0x8E && buf[k + 1] == 0x00) {
            int plen = buf[k + 2] | (buf[k + 3] << 8);
            if (plen > 4 && k + plen <= n) { printf("MAP: %-12s -> %.*s\n", any ? "" : what, plen - 4, buf + k + 4); any = 1; k += plen - 1; }
        }
    }
    if (!any && what[0] != '(') printf("MAP: %-12s -> (no answer)\n", what);
}

static SOCKET dial(const char *ip, int port)
{
    SOCKET s = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0);
    struct sockaddr_in a;
    u_long nb = 1;
    memset(&a, 0, sizeof a);
    a.sin_family = AF_INET;
    a.sin_port = htons((unsigned short)port);
    a.sin_addr.s_addr = inet_addr(ip);
    if (connect(s, (struct sockaddr *)&a, sizeof a) != 0) { printf("connect %s:%d failed %d\n", ip, port, WSAGetLastError()); return INVALID_SOCKET; }
    ioctlsocket(s, FIONBIO, &nb); /* like the game client */
    return s;
}

/* ---- tamper test stubs (detection tests only; they act on this test process and nothing else) ---- */
#include "MinHook.h"
static DWORD (WINAPI *real_tick)(void);
static BOOL (WINAPI *real_qpc)(LARGE_INTEGER *);
static int g_factor = 1;
static DWORD g_tick0;
static LONGLONG g_qpc0;
static DWORD WINAPI fast_tick(void) { DWORD t = real_tick(); return g_tick0 + (t - g_tick0) * (DWORD)g_factor; }
static BOOL WINAPI fast_qpc(LARGE_INTEGER *c)
{
    BOOL r = real_qpc(c);
    if (r) c->QuadPart = g_qpc0 + (c->QuadPart - g_qpc0) * g_factor;
    return r;
}

/* OG_SPEEDTEST=<factor>: time APIs of this process run <factor> times faster (speed-hack pattern) */
static void speed_test(int factor)
{
    LARGE_INTEGER q;
    HMODULE k = GetModuleHandleA("kernel32.dll");
    g_factor = factor;
    g_tick0 = GetTickCount();
    QueryPerformanceCounter(&q);
    g_qpc0 = q.QuadPart;
    if (MH_Initialize() != MH_OK ||
        MH_CreateHook((LPVOID)GetProcAddress(k, "GetTickCount"), (LPVOID)fast_tick, (LPVOID *)&real_tick) != MH_OK ||
        MH_CreateHook((LPVOID)GetProcAddress(k, "QueryPerformanceCounter"), (LPVOID)fast_qpc, (LPVOID *)&real_qpc) != MH_OK ||
        MH_EnableHook(MH_ALL_HOOKS) != MH_OK) { printf("speed test: hooks failed\n"); return; }
    printf("speed test: time x%d\n", factor);
}

/* OG_CODEPATCH=guard|exe: changes one code byte of a function that is never called in this process */
static void unused_function(void) { printf("never called\n"); }
static void code_patch(const char *what)
{
    unsigned char *p = !_stricmp(what, "guard") ? (unsigned char *)GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleA("odinguard.dll"), "OdinGuard_CanonDump")
                                                : (unsigned char *)unused_function;
    DWORD old;
    if (!p || !VirtualProtect(p, 1, PAGE_EXECUTE_READWRITE, &old)) { printf("code patch: failed\n"); return; }
    p[0] ^= 0x01;
    VirtualProtect(p, 1, old, &old);
    FlushInstructionCache(GetCurrentProcess(), p, 1);
    printf("code patch: one byte of the %s code changed\n", what);
}

int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    WSADATA wd;
    unsigned char pkt[55], buf[8192];
    SOCKET s;
    int n;
    unsigned id;
    if (argc < 5) { printf("usage: nettest <ip> <login-port> <user> <password> [char-port [map-port [char-name]]]\n"); return 2; }
    WSAStartup(0x0202, &wd);
    if (!LoadLibraryA("odinguard.dll")) printf("odinguard.dll not loaded (%lu), plain connection\n", GetLastError());

    s = dial(argv[1], atoi(argv[2]));
    if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) return 1;
    memset(pkt, 0, sizeof pkt);
    pkt[0] = 0x64; pkt[1] = 0x00;           /* CA_LOGIN */
    pkt[2] = 55;                             /* version */
    strncpy((char *)pkt + 6, argv[3], 24);
    strncpy((char *)pkt + 30, argv[4], 24);
    pkt[54] = 0;                             /* client type */
    if (send(s, (const char *)pkt, sizeof pkt, 0) != (int)sizeof pkt) { printf("send failed %d\n", WSAGetLastError()); return 1; }
    n = recv_some(s, buf, sizeof buf, 5000);
    if (n < 3) { printf("LOGIN: no answer (%d bytes, error %d)\n", n, WSAGetLastError()); return 1; }
    id = buf[0] | (buf[1] << 8);
    if (id == 0x006A || id == 0x083E) { printf("LOGIN: refused, code %d\n", buf[2]); closesocket(s); return 3; }
    if (id != 0x0069 && id != 0x0AC4) { printf("LOGIN: unexpected packet 0x%04X (%d bytes)\n", id, n); return 1; }
    {
        unsigned login1 = *(unsigned *)(buf + 4), account = *(unsigned *)(buf + 8), login2 = *(unsigned *)(buf + 12);
        unsigned char sex = buf[46];
        printf("LOGIN: accepted, packet 0x%04X, account %u\n", id, account);
        closesocket(s);
        if (argc > 5) {
            unsigned char c[17];
            s = dial(argv[1], atoi(argv[5]));
            if (s == INVALID_SOCKET) return 1;
            c[0] = 0x65; c[1] = 0;
            memcpy(c + 2, &account, 4); memcpy(c + 6, &login1, 4); memcpy(c + 10, &login2, 4);
            c[14] = 0; c[15] = 0; c[16] = sex;
            send(s, (const char *)c, sizeof c, 0);
            n = recv_some(s, buf, sizeof buf, 5000);
            if (n >= 4 && *(unsigned *)buf == account) {
                printf("CHAR: account id echoed, %d bytes total", n);
                if (n > 4) printf(", next packet 0x%04X", buf[4] | (buf[5] << 8));
                printf("\n");
            } else {
                printf("CHAR: unexpected answer (%d bytes)\n", n);
                return 1;
            }
            if (argc > 6) {
                /* select slot 0, then enter the map server and type the OdinGuard chat commands */
                unsigned char sel[3] = { 0x66, 0x00, 0 }, enter[19], ack[2] = { 0x7D, 0x00 };
                unsigned char *p = NULL;
                unsigned charid, mport, i;
                SOCKET m;
                send(s, (const char *)sel, 3, 0);
                n = recv_some(s, buf, sizeof buf, 8000);
                for (i = 0; i + 28 <= (unsigned)n; i++)
                    if ((buf[i] == 0x71 || buf[i] == 0xC5) && buf[i + 1] == (buf[i] == 0x71 ? 0x00 : 0x0A)) { p = buf + i; break; }
                if (!p) { printf("CHAR: no map server answer (%d bytes)\n", n); return 1; }
                charid = *(unsigned *)(p + 2);
                mport = p[26] | (p[27] << 8);
                printf("CHAR: char %u selected, map server port %u\n", charid, mport);
                closesocket(s);
                m = dial(argv[1], atoi(argv[6]));
                if (m == INVALID_SOCKET) return 1;
                enter[0] = 0x36; enter[1] = 0x04;
                memcpy(enter + 2, &account, 4); memcpy(enter + 6, &charid, 4); memcpy(enter + 10, &login1, 4);
                i = GetTickCount(); memcpy(enter + 14, &i, 4); enter[18] = sex;
                send(m, (const char *)enter, sizeof enter, 0);
                n = recv_some(m, buf, sizeof buf, 8000);
                printf("MAP: %d bytes after enter, first packet 0x%04X\n", n, n >= 2 ? buf[0] | (buf[1] << 8) : 0);
                send(m, (const char *)ack, 2, 0);
                recv_some(m, buf, sizeof buf, 2000);
                {
                    static const char *defcmds[] = { "!ping", "!vsync off", "!vsync on", "!crash" };
                    const char *cmds[16];
                    int c, ncmd = 0;
                    char envbuf[1024], *tok, *ctx = NULL;
                    /* OG_CHAT="cmd1;cmd2;..." replaces the default commands, OG_HOLD = seconds to stay afterwards */
                    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("OG_CHAT", envbuf, sizeof envbuf)) {
                        for (tok = strtok_r(envbuf, ";", &ctx); tok && ncmd < 16; tok = strtok_r(NULL, ";", &ctx)) cmds[ncmd++] = tok;
                    } else {
                        for (c = 0; c < 4; c++) cmds[ncmd++] = defcmds[c];
                    }
                    for (c = 0; c < ncmd; c++) {
                        char chat[160];
                        int len = snprintf(chat + 4, sizeof chat - 4, "%s : %s", argc > 7 ? argv[7] : "OgTester", cmds[c]) + 5;
                        chat[0] = (char)0xF3; chat[1] = 0; chat[2] = (char)len; chat[3] = 0;
                        send(m, chat, len, 0);
                        n = recv_some(m, buf, sizeof buf, 2500);
                        print_messages(cmds[c], buf, n);
                    }
                    /* OG_SKILLSPAM=n: n First Aid requests on yourself without waiting (no-delay pattern) */
                    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("OG_SKILLSPAM", envbuf, sizeof envbuf)) {
                        int i, cnt = atoi(envbuf);
                        unsigned char sk[10] = { 0x38, 0x04, 1, 0, 142, 0 };
                        memcpy(sk + 6, &account, 4);
                        for (i = 0; i < cnt; i++) { send(m, (const char *)sk, 10, 0); Sleep(20); }
                        n = recv_some(m, buf, sizeof buf, 1500);
                        printf("MAP: skillspam %d sent\n", cnt);
                    }
                    /* OG_FLOOD=n: n packets as fast as possible (rate limit) */
                    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("OG_FLOOD", envbuf, sizeof envbuf)) {
                        int i, cnt = atoi(envbuf);
                        unsigned char act[7] = { 0x37, 0x04, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0 };
                        memcpy(act + 2, &account, 4);
                        for (i = 0; i < cnt; i++) { if (send(m, (const char *)act, 7, 0) <= 0) break; if (i % 50 == 0) Sleep(200); }
                        printf("MAP: flood %d sent\n", i);
                    }
                    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("OG_SPEEDTEST", envbuf, sizeof envbuf) && atoi(envbuf) > 1) speed_test(atoi(envbuf));
                    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("OG_CODEPATCH", envbuf, sizeof envbuf)) {
                        char *e = envbuf + strlen(envbuf);
                        while (e > envbuf && (e[-1] == ' ' || e[-1] == '\t')) *--e = 0;   /* cmd "set X=v &" keeps the space */
                        code_patch(envbuf);
                    }
                    /* OG_ATTACK=1: attack the honeypot unit (only a bot would) */
                    if (GetEnvironmentVariableA("OG_ATTACK", envbuf, sizeof envbuf)) {
                        unsigned char act[7] = { 0x37, 0x04 };
                        unsigned int id = 0x7A000000u | (account & 0xFFFFFF);
                        memcpy(act + 2, &id, 4);
                        act[6] = 0;
                        send(m, (const char *)act, 7, 0);
                        printf("MAP: attacked honeypot %08x\n", id);
                    }
                }
                {
                    char hold[16];
                    /* keep reading like the game does: the guard answers challenges and pings inside recv() */
                    /* wall clock: the speed test changes GetTickCount of this process */
                    ULONGLONG end = wall_ms() + (GetEnvironmentVariableA("OG_HOLD", hold, sizeof hold) ? atoi(hold) * 1000 : 6000);
                    while (wall_ms() < end) {
                        n = recv_some(m, buf, sizeof buf, 500);
                        if (n > 0) print_messages("(hold)", buf, n);
                    }
                }
                closesocket(m);
                {   /* OG_CANON=<file>: write the guard's canonical image after the session (self-integrity diagnostics) */
                    char path[MAX_PATH];
                    int (*dump)(const char *) = (int (*)(const char *))GetProcAddress(GetModuleHandleA("odinguard.dll"), "OdinGuard_CanonDump");
                    if (dump && GetEnvironmentVariableA("OG_CANON", path, sizeof path)) printf("canon dump: %d\n", dump(path));
                }
            } else {
                Sleep(1500);
                closesocket(s);
            }
        }
    }
    return 0;
}
```

`client/tests/selftest.c`:

```c
#include <windows.h>
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

typedef int (*report_fn)(char *, size_t);

/* Loads odinguard.dll from the current directory and prints its report. */
int main(int argc, char **argv)
{
    HMODULE m = LoadLibraryA("odinguard.dll");
    report_fn rep;
    char *buf;
    int n;
        if (!m) { printf("load failed: %lu\n", GetLastError()); return 1; }
    rep = (report_fn)GetProcAddress(m, "OdinGuard_Report");
    buf = malloc(1 << 20);
    n = rep(buf, 1 << 20);
    fwrite(buf, 1, n, stdout);
    if (argc > 2 && !strcmp(argv[1], "canon")) {
        int (*dump)(const char *) = (int (*)(const char *))GetProcAddress(m, "OdinGuard_CanonDump");
        printf("canon dump %s: %d\n", argv[2], dump ? dump(argv[2]) : -1);
    }
    if (argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "crash")) ((void (*)(void))GetProcAddress(m, "OdinGuard_CrashNow"))();
    Sleep(500);
    if (argc > 1 && !strcmp(argv[1], "hold")) Sleep(6000);
    return 0;
}
```

`docs/01-muhro-reference-analysis.md`:

```md
# 01 – Reference analysis: how a modern RO client guard is bound (MuhRO)

Scope: structure and binding only. No keys, protocol constants or detection
lists were extracted, and none will be copied. Analysis date 2026-11-23, files
copied read-only from the VM (`C:\muh\MuhRO`) to the git-ignored `analysis/_bin/`.

Note: MuhRO does **not** ship a `gepard.dll`. It uses its own guard (`MuhExt.dll`,
internal name "MuhGuard"). It is still a good example of a current 2018+ design
and shows the same binding pattern as Gepard.

## 1. Files and roles

| File | Size | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `Muh.exe` | 49.8 MB | Game client. Themida-protected (`.themida`, `.boot`, `.scrt`), signed (Authenticode), has TLS callbacks. |
| `MuhExt.dll` | 4 MB | The guard and extensions. **Statically imported by the exe** (string `MuhExt.dll` is in the exe's import table), so the loader maps it before game code runs. |
| `ijl15.dll` (9.7 KB) | – | Small proxy of the Intel JPEG lib. Reads `dinput.ini` (ROExt settings) and forwards to `ijl15x.dll` (the real one). Classic extension hook, unrelated to the guard. |
| `v3hunt.dll`, `mguard1.dat`, `mguard2.dat`, `muhguard-reject-paths.v1` | – | Data and AV helper. The reject-path list is a server-supplied deny list for resource paths. |
| `muhvault-current.mvm` + `.sig` + `muhvault-signing.public` | 338 MB | Signed asset container. Public key shipped, signature checked at start. |
| `plugin.ini` | 5 KB | LGP (Lite Graphics Plugin): per-skill ground-cell images and fade times. |
| `GRF.INI` | – | Plain GRF load order: `custom.grf`, `addons.grf`, `muh-generated.grf`, `muh.grf`. |
| `Muh_Patcher.exe` | 18 MB | Patcher / launcher. |
| `ddraw.dll` (8.9 MB), `dxvk.conf`, `dgVoodoo.conf` | – | Graphics wrapper. |

## 2. Binding mechanism

```
Muh_Patcher.exe  --(starts)-->  Muh.exe
                                  │ Windows loader resolves imports
                                  ▼
   basesdk.dll, iapsdk.dll, binkw32.dll, granny2.dll, …, MuhExt.dll   (static imports)
                                  │ DLL init (DllMain, TLS callbacks)
                                  ▼
   MuhExt.dll exports a versioned C ABI (35 symbols, suffix V1/V2/V3), e.g.
     MuhGuardImportBind_<hash>        <- bind function; hash differs per build
     MuhGuardRouteNativeInboundV1     <- inbound packet routing
     MuhVaultAcquireClientBridgeV3
```

Key facts:

1. **Binding is an import-table patch of the exe**, not injection. `MuhExt.dll`
   is a normal static dependency, so the loader maps it before any game code.
   No `CreateRemoteThread`/`LoadLibrary` injection, which is robust against
   launchers and compatibility layers.
2. **Two-way coupling.** The exe imports DLL functions and the DLL hooks the exe
   (Detours sections `.detourc/.detourd`). The per-build hash in the bind export
   name means a swapped DLL does not fit another build.
3. **Versioned ABI** (`…V1`, `…V3`): the exe uses a small stable surface, so the guard
   can be updated independently.
4. **Network protocol** has its own namespaces inside the DLL (hello with build +
   device fingerprint, framed and keyed messages in the normal game connection,
   crash reports with a schema version).
5. HTTP (`winhttp`) for updates/reports; signature checks via `wintrust`/`crypt32`/`bcrypt`.

## 3. Reference client (2018-06-20 Sakray)

* `alpha.exe`: 32-bit, packed/patched, no guard imports.
* `client-dev/ragnarok/ijl15.dll` is already an **ROExt proxy** (from muhRO, config
  `dinput.ini`), original renamed to `ijl15x.dll`. The exe loads it by name, so we
  have a guaranteed load point **without touching the exe**.
* GRFs are read through `DATA.INI` (`cdata.grf` first).

## 4. Consequences for OdinGuard

* Load point 1 (now): own proxy DLL named `ijl15.dll` that chains to `ijl15x.dll`
  and loads `odinguard.dll` (reversible, no exe patch).
* Load point 2 (hardening): import-table patch of the exe so the guard is mapped
  before any game code and cannot be removed by deleting the proxy.
* Keep a small versioned export ABI between loader and guard.
* Per-build bind name/secret.
* Server authority: the DLL collects and reports, the server decides.

```

`docs/02-architecture.md`:

```md
# 02 – Architektur von OdinGuard Anti Cheat 1.0

Kennzeichnung: **[gemessen]** = selbst gebaut/getestet, **[gelesen]** = aus Code/Doku belegt,
**[vermutet]** = plausibel, nicht geprüft, **[Vorschlag]** = Empfehlung.

## 1. Grundsätze

1. **Der Server entscheidet.** Ein Client kann nicht beweisen, dass er ehrlich ist. Echte Sicherheit kommt nur aus
   serverseitigen Prüfungen (Ratenlimits, Delay, Plausibilität, Handshake-Pflicht, Bans). Alles im Client ist eine
   **Hürde**: es macht Manipulation teurer und erkennbar und liefert Belege (Abschnitt 9).
2. **Offener Code, geheime Schlüssel.** Sicherheit beruht auf Schlüsseln pro Server (Server-Schlüssel, Build-Secret,
   Signier-Schlüssel) und auf Build-Variation pro Betreiber, nicht auf geheimem Code.
3. **Ein Profil, ein Release.** `odinguard.profile.toml` ist die einzige Quelle. Studio (GUI) und `og` (CLI) bauen
   daraus dasselbe signierte Release. Geheimnisse stehen nie im Profil, nur ihre Dateipfade.
4. **Modular zur Build-Zeit.** Nicht gewählte Module sind nicht im Binary (Beleg: Linker-Map, Abschnitt 2.3).
5. **Flaggen, dann verzögert bannen.** Detections erzeugen Flags mit Punkten; Bans kommen gesammelt in Ban-Wellen,
   damit Cheater die auslösende Prüfung nicht zuordnen können.
6. **Keine Fehlalarme als Ziel.** Jede Regel hat Schwere, Konfidenz und Aktion (log, flag, flagban, kick, ban);
   Allowlist für legitime Add-ons; Rollout beginnt im Warnmodus.

## 2. Modulsystem

### 2.1 Registry (`modules/modules.toml`) [gelesen]

Jedes Modul hat `id`, `version`, `kind` (core, protection, detection, challenge, gameplay, client-feature), `side`
(client, server, both), `requires` (Abhängigkeiten), `client_src` (C-Quellen im Client), `define`
(`OG_MOD_*` im generierten `og_modules.h`), `server_key` (Schalter in `odinguard_athena.conf`), `assets`
(Gruppen für `odin.grf`) und `param` (Name, Typ, Default, Min/Max, Konfig-Schlüssel, Hilfetext).

| Modul | Art | Seite | braucht | Client-Quellen | Server-Schalter | Parameter |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| core | core | beide | – | og_main, og_log, og_net, og_sha256, og_challenge, og_wire | og_enable | required, log_only, min_version |
| rate-limit | protection | Server | – | – | og_rate_limit | packets_per_second, action |
| hwid | protection | beide | core | og_hwid | og_hwid | ban_match |
| multi-client | protection | beide | hwid | og_env | og_multi_client | max_per_machine, max_windows, block_vm, vm_action |
| heartbeat | protection | beide | core | og_guard | og_heartbeat | interval, timeout |
| integrity | protection | beide | heartbeat | og_integrity | og_integrity | action, tamper_action |
| cheat-signatures | detection | beide | heartbeat | og_detect | og_signatures | package, inject_action |
| grf-rules | protection | beide | heartbeat | og_assets | og_grf_rules | strict, action (+ GRF-Manifest aus `[grf]`) |
| input-filter | protection | beide | heartbeat | og_input | og_input_filter | enabled |
| crash-report | client-feature | Client | core | og_crash | – | – |
| client-commands | client-feature | beide | core | og_cmds | og_client_commands | – |
| colors | gameplay | beide | core | og_text, og_ui | og_colors | – |
| branding | client-feature | Client | core | og_splash | – | – |
| lgp | gameplay | Server | core | – | og_lgp_enable | – |
| ban-system | protection | Server | core | – | og_ban_system | wave_hour, ban_score |
| behaviour | detection | Server | ban-system | – | og_behaviour | nodelay_per_minute, autopot_ms, macro_jitter_ms |
| ch-nonce | challenge | beide | core | (core) | og_ch_nonce | interval, action |
| ch-code | challenge | beide | integrity | (core) | og_ch_code | interval, action |
| ch-time | challenge | beide | core | (core) | og_ch_time | interval, max_drift_percent, action |
| ch-file | challenge | beide | core | (core) | og_ch_file | interval, action |
| ch-captcha | challenge | Server | behaviour | – | og_ch_captcha | action |
| ch-honeypot | challenge | Server | ban-system | – | og_ch_honeypot | action |
| competitive-pack | gameplay | beide | ch-file | – | og_competitive_pack | – |

### 2.2 Build-Zeit und Laufzeit

- **Build-Zeit (Client):** Das Studio schreibt `og_modules.h` (`#define OG_MOD_* 1` nur für gewählte Module),
  `og_modules.mk` (Liste der C-Quellen) und `og_profile.h` (Betreiber, Ports, Salts, Server-Public-Key,
  geschützte Dateien – Geheimnisse XOR-maskiert mit `BLAKE2b("OdinGuard/mask" ‖ seed ‖ id)`). Nicht gewählte
  Module sind in `og.h` leere `static inline`-Stubs. Die Link-Reihenfolge wird mit dem Seed gemischt.
- **Laufzeit (Server):** `odinguard_athena.conf` + `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt` (vom Studio generiert) schalten
  Module und Parameter; der Server schickt die Policy (OG_S_POLICY) und das Signaturpaket (OG_S_SIGS) nach dem
  Handshake. Spätere Zeilen überschreiben frühere (`og_switch_set`).
- **Abhängigkeiten:** Das Studio schließt die Hülle (`requires`) und lehnt Profile mit fehlenden Abhängigkeiten,
  Parametern außerhalb Min/Max oder unbekannten Modulen ab (`og validate`, Unit-Test `validation_catches_errors`).

### 2.3 Beleg „nicht gewählter Code steckt nicht im Binary“ [gemessen]

`client/Makefile` erzeugt ein Objekt pro Quelle unter `OUT/obj/` und eine Linker-Map. Die Pipeline liest die
Map (`linked_objects`) und bricht ab, wenn ein nicht gewähltes Modulobjekt gelinkt wurde (`check_linked`).
Messung 2026-11-23: Minimal-Profil (core + rate-limit) linkt 6 Kern-Objekte, DLL 271 360 Byte, keine Strings
anderer Module; Default-Profil 1 026 560 Byte.

## 3. Profil (`odinguard.profile.toml`, Schema 3)

Abschnitte: `modules`, `[general]` (id, operator, client_build, ports, splash_ms, variation_seed, hwid_salt),
`[keys]` (Pfade: server_seed, signing_seed, build_secret), `[params.<modul>]`, `[commands.<id>]` (enabled, name,
group, rate_ms), `[signatures]` (sources, allowlist, max_action, version), `[assets]` (competitive_pack,
odin_grf-Gruppen, competitive_source + competitive = Pack-Kategorien), `[grf]` (GRF-Manifest: `file`, `mod`,
`overlays`, Aktionen), `[signatures.groups]` (pro Tool-Gruppe `off` oder Aktion), `signatures.disabled`, `output`,
`[rollout]` (stage 1–4, reviewed_rules).
Migration: `profile::migrate` hebt Schema 1 → 2 → 3 an (3: Auren raus, sie sind jetzt ein eigenes rAthena-Feature;
Test `schema1_profile_migrates_without_data_loss`),
`og migrate` legt eine `.bak`-Kopie an.

Ableitungen (Studio, `pipeline::Derived`):
- `proto_salt = BLAKE2b-128("OdinGuard/proto-salt" ‖ variation_seed ‖ server_pub)`
- `profile_tag = BLAKE2b-128("OdinGuard/tag" ‖ proto_salt)` – ein Client eines fremden Profils wird mit Status 3
  abgewiesen [gemessen, E2E].
- Secrets für den Server landen in `secrets/odinguard.env` (`ODINGUARD_KEY`, `ODINGUARD_PROTO_SALT`,
  `ODINGUARD_BUILD_SECRET`).

## 4. Protokoll v2 (`proto/og_proto.h`, `og_wire.c`)

- Handshake: Client-Hello (X25519 ephemer, Nonce, Version, Build, Hardware-Komponenten, `profile_tag`) → Server-
  Antwort mit Ed25519-Signatur über das Transkript; der Client prüft gegen den **eingebauten** Server-Key.
- KDF: `BLAKE2b-512("OdinGuard/v2" ‖ proto_salt ‖ shared ‖ pubs ‖ nonces)` → je ein Schlüssel pro Richtung.
- Records: XChaCha20-Poly1305 über den **gesamten** Spielstrom, Zähler-Nonce (Replay/Reorder = Abbruch),
  Schlüsselrotation alle 4096 Records (`key = BLAKE2b-256(key ‖ "OdinGuard/rekey")`).
- Downgrade-Schutz: Client verweigert Server < v2, Server erzwingt `og_min_version ≥ 2`.
- Steuer-Nachrichten: C→S `ALIVE`, `DETECT`, `PONG`, `REPORT`, `RESPONSE`; S→C `POLICY`, `PING`, `COMMAND`,
  `COLORS`, `CHALLENGE`, `SIGS`.
- Parser sind reine Funktionen (`og_wire.c`, im Client und Server byte-identisch) und werden gefuzzt
  (`make -C client fuzz`: 2 000 000 Iterationen ASan/UBSan ohne Befund [gemessen]).
- Vergleiche von MACs/Digests in konstanter Zeit (`crypto_verify16/32`, Monocypher).

## 5. Challenge-Framework

Der Server schickt `OG_S_CHALLENGE {id, type, nonce[16], target, a, b}` in zufälligen Abständen
(`interval` ± Zufallsfenster); der Client antwortet mit `OG_C_RESPONSE`. Jede Challenge-ID gilt einmal
(Antwort auf unbekannte/beantwortete ID = `challenge:replay`), Timeout = Fehlschlag.

| Challenge | Prüft | Server kennt | Schutzwirkung |
|---|---|---|---|
| ch-nonce | `BLAKE2b(key = build_secret, "OG/nonce" ‖ nonce)` | Build-Secret | Hürde: beweist den Betreiber-Build, solange das Secret nicht aus dem RAM gezogen wird |
| ch-code | Hash eines zufälligen Bereichs des kanonischen Code-Images von Exe oder Guard | Referenz-Images (`conf/odinguard/`) | Hürde: Patches im Code fallen auf, auch wenn die Heartbeat-Hashes gefälscht werden |
| ch-time | Client-Uhr gegen Server-Uhr (Tick + Performance-Counter) | eigene Uhr | Hürde gegen Speedhacks; Server-Delay-Prüfung ist die echte Sicherheit |
| ch-file | Hash eines zufälligen Bereichs von `odin.grf` / Competitive-Pack | offizielle Dateien | Hürde, Pflichtdatei fehlt = Fehlschlag, optionale fehlt = ok |
| ch-captcha | Bot-Captcha nach Verhaltens-Flags, nie auf WoE/BG-Maps | Antwort | echte Sicherheit gegen unbeaufsichtigte Bots |
| ch-honeypot | unsichtbare Lockvogel-Einheit, die nur Bots angreifen | Einheiten-ID | echte Sicherheit (serverseitig), Treffer = flagban |

Kanonisches Image: nicht beschreibbare, nicht verwerfbare Sektionen; HIGHLOW-Relocations und die IAT
(Datenverzeichnis 12) genullt, damit ASLR und Loader-Schreibzugriffe den Hash nicht ändern [gemessen].
Fehlschläge gehen über `og_report` → Flag mit Punkten → Aktion laut Profil; Telemetrie nur Diagnose
(Regel, Zeit, Account, gehashte HWID).

## 6. Detection-Modul „cheat-signatures“

- **Quellen:** `signatures/signatures.toml` (300 Signaturen in 21 Tool-Gruppen, davon 164 vom Client prüfbar;
  statische Analyse der Proben plus öffentlich bekannte Tools, `analysis/cheat-signatures/`) und
  `signatures/allowlist.toml` (ROExt-Standard, dxwrapper, Skins, Overlays, Browser, Hersteller-Software).
- **Konfiguration:** Gruppe = ID-Präfix (`OG-RCX-001` → RCX). Profil `[signatures.groups]`: `off` oder eine Aktion
  für die ganze Gruppe; `signatures.disabled` für einzelne IDs; `og sig-groups` / Studio-Tab „Signaturen“.
- **Paket:** Das Studio kompiliert daraus `odinguard.sigpack` – `"OGSP"`, Version, Einträge
  `{id, kind, action, score, name, pattern}`, EdDSA-Signatur (Signier-Schlüssel des Profils). Der Server lädt es
  nur mit gültiger Signatur und Mindestversion und schickt die client-prüfbaren Arten an den Client.
- **Arten:** process, window_title, window_class, module, file_name, file_sha256, driver, grf_sha256, mutex
  (benannte Mutexe/Events/Sections), registry (Schlüssel vorhanden, HKCU/HKLM, 32/64-Bit-Sicht) – vom Client
  geprüft; grf_entry, import_pattern, string_pattern nur Analysedaten; allow_sha256, allow_path (Allowlist).
- **Punkte:** Schwere (low 10, medium 30, high 60, critical 100) × Konfidenz (high 1, medium 0,6, low 0,3);
  `max_action` des Profils kappt Aktionen (log < flag < flagban < kick < ban).
- **Verhalten (Server, echte Sicherheit):** `behaviour` – Skill-Anfragen innerhalb des Delays (nodelay),
  Autopot-Reaktionszeit, Makro-Timing; `rate-limit` – Pakete pro Sekunde (WPE/RPE-Sendeschleifen).
- **Fehlalarm-Schutz:** zwei Scans zur Bestätigung (Integrität), Allowlist vor jeder Meldung, Toleranzpfade
  (Warsaw, Treiber-Overlays, Parallels), jede Meldung einmal pro Verbindung [gemessen, `dettest`].

## 6a. GRF-Prüfung (Modul grf-rules, wie Gepard, aber patcher-tauglich)

- Der Server schickt mit dem Signaturpaket das GRF-Manifest des Betreibers (Arten `GRF_LIST`, `GRF_MOD`, `OVERLAY`).
- Der Guard prüft jede GRF aus `DATA.INI`: Name + Größe + **Tail-Hash** (SHA-256 über den 46-Byte-Header und die
  Dateitabelle bis Dateiende; jedes Umpacken oder Ändern eines Eintrags ändert die Tabelle) bei jedem Scan, gecacht
  nach Größe/Änderungszeit; der **Voll-Hash** der Datei läuft einmal im Hintergrund-Thread mit niedriger Priorität.
- Erlaubte Mods (`grf.mod`) werden über den Tail-Hash unabhängig vom Namen erkannt (Skins, darkworld-Varianten).
- Meldungen `grf:modified` (Tabelle oder Inhalt), `grf:unknown`, `grf:missing` (nur Pflicht-GRFs) mit eigener Aktion.
- Patcher: mehrere Versionen pro Name erlaubt (`og grf-scan --keep-previous`): erst Server-Konfig mit alter + neuer
  Version ausrollen, dann patchen, später alte Version entfernen. `odin.grf`/`odin-dark.grf` trägt jeder Build ein.
- Lose Dateien (`grf_strict`): außerhalb der Overlay-Ordner (eingebaut + `grf.overlays`) gemeldet.
- Grenzen: Wer den Guard selbst manipuliert, kann falsche Antworten liefern; serverseitig gegengeprüft wird
  stichprobenartig mit `ch-file` (zufällige Bereiche der offiziellen Dateien).

## 7. Command-Registry (`modules/commands.toml`)

13 Commands (3 Client `!…`, 10 Server `@…`) mit `id`, `kind`, `name` (umbenennbar), `module`, `group`
(Mindest-Gruppe), `rate_ms`, `params`, `help_de/en`. Das Studio erzeugt daraus:
- die Server-Konfig (`og_cmd_<id>`, `og_cmdgroup_<id>`, `og_cmdrate_<id>`, `og_cmdname_<id>`); deaktivierte
  Commands werden nicht registriert. Auch die `!`-Commands prüft der Map-Server (Registry in `og_map.cpp`:
  Name, Gruppe, Ratenlimit) und schickt dann `OG_S_COMMAND`/`OG_S_PING` an den Guard – der Client braucht
  keine eigene Tabelle, Umbenennen wirkt ohne Client-Update;
- die Doku (`og docs <profil> --lang de|en`, Release `docs/commands-*.md`; Abschnitt in `16-commands-referenz.md`).
Commands eines nicht gewählten Moduls sind automatisch aus.

## 8. OdinGuard Studio (`studio/`)

- `crates/og-core`: registry, profile (Schema + Migration), keys, crypto (Monocypher-FFI), sigpack, grf, generate,
  pipeline (Build), manifest (signiertes Hash-Manifest), update (Updater), rollout (Stufen-Gate).
- `crates/og-cli` (`og`): new, validate, registry, show, migrate, preview, build, verify-release, sigpack,
  sigpack-verify, sig-groups, grf-scan, grf-allow, grf-hash, keys, docs, rollout, update, update-manifest,
  update-verify.
- `apps/studio` (Tauri 2): Tabs Profil, Module & Challenges, Commands, Signaturen, GRF & Mods, Competitive-Pack,
  Build, Rollout, Updates; ruft nur
  og-core auf.
- **Release pro Profil** (`og build`): `client/` (odinguard.dll, ijl15.dll, odin.grf, [odin-dark.grf],
  odinguard.ini, README.txt, Lizenzen), `server/` (src, conf inkl. sigpack und Referenz-Images, sql),
  `patcher/filelist.txt`, `docs/` (Handbuch, Command-Referenz, Build-Report), `secrets/odinguard.env`,
  `manifest.json` + `manifest.sig` + `signing.pub`. `og verify-release` prüft Signatur und jede Datei.
- Reproduzierbar: gleiche Eingaben → gleiche Hashes (zweimal gebaut, identisch [gemessen]); Cross-Compile mit
  mingw-w64 auf macOS. Liegt das Ausgabeverzeichnis auf einem Pfad mit Leerzeichen, baut die Pipeline den
  Client in einem festen Arbeitsordner unter `$TMPDIR/odinguard-build/<id>` (GNU make kann keine Leerzeichen).

## 9. odin.grf

Nur Assets (LGP-Kacheln `hanmoon1/2.tga`, später UI), gebaut mit `rgrf-core` aus den Asset-Gruppen der
gewählten Module und danach mit `rgrf_core::verify` geprüft. DLLs und Server-Code liegen nie in der GRF.
`odin.grf` ist Pflicht-Datei der `ch-file`-Challenge, das Competitive-Pack (`odin-dark.grf`) optional.
Ladereihenfolge (`DATA.INI`): `0=odin.grf`, `1=odin-dark.grf` (falls gewählt), danach die GRFs des Clients.
Competitive-Pack: aus wählbaren Kategorien (`assets/competitive/recipe.toml`, Staging-Ordner pro Kategorie) oder
einer fertigen GRF; alle Spieler bekommen dasselbe Pack.

## 10. Updater und Rollout

- **Studio-Selbstupdate:** Kanäle `stable`/`beta`, Endpunkt `<basis>/<kanal>.json` + `.sig`; Standard: GitHub
  Releases des OdinGuard-Repos (stable = neuestes Release, beta = Release mit Tag `beta`), per
  `OG_STUDIO_UPDATE_ENDPOINT` überschreibbar. Schritt 1 (og-core):
  Manifest-Signatur (minisign), Downgrade-Sperre gegen die höchste je akzeptierte Version, Pinning des
  Manifest-Hashes. Schritt 2 (Tauri-Updater-Plugin, gleicher Endpunkt): Artefakt-Signatur und Installation.
  Nur https (http nur Loopback in Tests). Privater Schlüssel `keys/studio-updater.key` bleibt lokal.
- **Core-/Signatur-Updates:** `og update --key core|sigpack …` lädt, prüft und legt Versionen unter
  `versions/<key>/<version>/` ab; `--rollback` schaltet auf die vorige lokal gehaltene Version.
- **Release-Pipeline:** `tools/release_studio.sh <stable|beta> <https-basis>` baut, signiert Artefakt und
  Manifest, prüft offline (`og update-verify`) und veröffentlicht **nichts**.
- **Rollout-Stufen pro Profil:** 1 Warnmodus (`log_only`) → 2 Kick → 3 Patcher-Auslieferung → 4 Pflicht
  (`required`). `og rollout` liest Exporte von `og_event`/`og_client` und sperrt Stufe 4, solange Regeln mit
  Fehlalarm-Verdacht (Quote über `fp_percent`) ungeprüft sind oder zu wenige aktive Accounts den Guard nutzen.

## 11. Härtung: Hürde oder echte Sicherheit

| Maßnahme | Wo | Wirkung | Stand |
|---|---|---|---|
| AEAD über den ganzen Strom, Sitzungsschlüssel, Replay-Schutz, Rekey | beide | echte Sicherheit gegen Mitlesen/Einschleusen im Netz; Hürde gegen Tools im Prozess | gemessen (E2E) |
| Gepinnter Server-Key, signierte Policy/Sigpack, Downgrade-Schutz | beide | echte Sicherheit gegen MITM und gefälschte Server-Daten | gemessen |
| Profil-Tag / Protokoll-Salt pro Betreiber | beide | Hürde: Clients/Bypässe für einen Server laufen nicht auf einem anderen | gemessen |
| Parser-Fuzzing | beide | echte Sicherheit gegen Speicherfehler in den Parsern | gemessen |
| ASLR, DEP, Stack-Protector, keine Timestamps | Client | Hürde, erschwert Exploits | gelesen (Makefile) |
| CFG (Control Flow Guard) | Client | Hürde gegen Code-Umlenkung; mit llvm-mingw (`TOOLCHAIN=llvm`, `OG_TOOLCHAIN=llvm og build`), mingw-gcc kann es nicht | gemessen: GuardFlags gesetzt (REA), Laufzeit siehe 05-tests |
| String-Maskierung, Build-Variation (Link-Reihenfolge, Konstanten) | Client | Hürde gegen generische Patches | gemessen (Hashes je Profil verschieden) |
| Anti-Debug, Hardware-Breakpoints, API-Hook-Check, Selbst-Integrität | Client | Hürde, zweistufig bestätigt | gemessen (keine Fehlalarme im Testclient) |
| Code-Signing (Authenticode) | Client | senkt AV-Fehlalarme | Hook vorgesehen, kein Zertifikat |
| Challenges nonce/code/time/file | beide | Hürde mit serverseitiger Prüfung | gemessen (E2E) |
| Rate-Limit, Delay/Nodelay, Honeypot, Captcha, Multi-Client, Handshake-Pflicht | Server | **echte Sicherheit** | gemessen (E2E, Captcha nur Server-Logik) |
| Flags, Ban-Wellen, Audit-Log (`og_event`, `og_flag`) | Server | echte Sicherheit + Nachvollziehbarkeit | gemessen |
| GRF-Allowlist (offizielle Hashes, ch-file) | beide | Hürde; serverseitig geprüft | gemessen |

Ehrlich: Wer den Rechner kontrolliert (Kernel-Treiber, VM-Introspektion, eigener Loader ohne Guard + gestohlenes
Build-Secret), kann jede Client-Prüfung umgehen. Ziel ist, öffentliche Tools und Bots zu stoppen und Handarbeit
teuer und nachweisbar zu machen; serverseitige Regeln greifen unabhängig vom Client.

## 12. ADR: Sprachen

| Teil | Sprache | Begründung |
|---|---|---|
| Client-DLL, Loader | C11 (mingw-w64, 32 Bit) | klein (271 KB minimal), AV-freundlich, kein Runtime-Ballast, Hooks/Win32-FFI ohnehin `unsafe`; getestet seit v0.1 |
| Server-Modul | C++ (xAthena) | nativ im Emulator, gleiche Build-Kette |
| Gemeinsame Parser | C (`og_wire.c`), in beiden byte-identisch | eine Implementierung, gefuzzt |
| Studio, CLI, Signatur-/Manifest-/Update-Werkzeuge | Rust (Tauri 2) | Speichersicherheit beim Parsen fremder Daten, Cross-Platform-GUI, RustyGRF-Crates direkt nutzbar |

Keine Abweichung von der Standardannahme in `<architecture>` Punkt 6.

```

`docs/03-integration.md`:

```md
# 03 – Einbindung beim Betreiber

Grundsatz: Es gibt kein Spieler-Setup und kein Spieler-`uninstall`. OdinGuard kommt nur über das Release des
Betreibers (Studio/`og build`) und dessen Patcher zum Spieler.

## 1. Profil anlegen und bauen

1. `og new <name>.profile.toml --id <id> --operator "<Servername>"` – legt Profil, Server-Schlüssel, Signier-
   Schlüssel und Build-Secret an (Dateien bleiben lokal, nie committen, sichern).
2. Module, Parameter, Commands, Auren und Signaturquellen im Studio oder direkt im TOML wählen; `og validate`.
3. `og build <profil>` → Release-Ordner (Inhalt siehe `docs/02-architecture.md` §8); `og verify-release <ordner>`.
4. Bestehende Installation weiterführen: `hwid_salt` und `server_seed` **nie ändern** (sonst verlieren alle
   Rechner-Sperren ihre Wirkung bzw. ausgelieferte Clients passen nicht mehr zum Server).

## 2. Client

1. Der vorhandene `ijl15.dll` des Clients (z. B. ROExt) wird zu `ijl15r.dll`; der OdinGuard-Loader wird
   `ijl15.dll`. Ladekette: `<exe> → ijl15.dll (Loader) → ijl15r.dll (ROExt) → ijl15x.dll`, zusätzlich lädt der
   Loader `odinguard.dll`.
2. `odin.grf` (und optional `odin-dark.grf`) in `DATA.INI` **vor** den übrigen GRFs eintragen:
   `0=odin.grf`, `1=odin-dark.grf`, danach die bisherigen Einträge.
3. Alle Dateien aus `client/` plus `ijl15r.dll` in die Pflichtliste des Patchers aufnehmen
   (`patcher/filelist.txt` enthält Namen und SHA-256).
4. `odinguard.ini` ist optional (Splash-Dauer, Debug-Log).

## 3. Server (rAthena/xAthena)

1. `server/src/*` in den Emulator kopieren, Hook-Zeilen laut `server/HOOKS.txt` (Repository) setzen, bauen
   (`og_wire.c` muss in `COMMON_H` stehen, sonst baut make das Objekt bei Änderungen nicht neu).
2. `server/conf/odinguard_athena.conf`, `server/conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt` und `server/conf/odinguard/`
   (Signaturpaket, Referenz-Images von Guard und GRFs) nach `conf/` kopieren.
3. Die drei Werte aus `secrets/odinguard.env` als Umgebungsvariablen setzen (`ODINGUARD_KEY`,
   `ODINGUARD_PROTO_SALT`, `ODINGUARD_BUILD_SECRET`) oder in `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt` eintragen – nie in git.
4. Tabellen (`og_client`, `og_component`, `og_ban`, `og_event`, `og_flag`, `og_aura_unlock`) entstehen beim ersten
   Start (`CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, `server/sql/odinguard.sql` zum Nachlesen).
5. Aura-Quests: `npc/added/odinguard_auras.txt` in `npc/scripts_added.conf` eintragen, Quest-IDs in
   `db/import/quest_db.yml` (Questlog-Texte brauchen Einträge in der Client-Lub).

## 4. Rollout-Stufen (im Profil, `[rollout] stage`)

| Stufe | Server-Schalter | Wirkung | Weiter, wenn |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Warnmodus | `og_required: no`, `og_log_only: yes` | alles wird nur protokolliert; Flags werden gesammelt, Ban-Welle läuft trocken | `og rollout` zeigt keine ungeprüften Regeln über der Fehlalarm-Schwelle |
| 2 Kick | `og_log_only: no` | Aktionen greifen (Kick, Flag, Ban-Welle), Spieler ohne Guard spielen weiter | Fehlalarm-Quote bleibt niedrig |
| 3 Patcher | wie 2 | Guard wird an alle Spieler ausgeliefert | Abdeckung (Accounts mit Guard) hoch genug |
| 4 Pflicht | `og_required: yes` | ohne gültigen Guard kein Login | – |

`og rollout <profil> --events og_event.tsv --clients og_client.tsv [--active N] [--advance]` (oder Tab „Rollout“
im Studio) prüft das Gate; nach `--advance` Release neu bauen und die Server-Konfig ausrollen.

## 5. Updates

- Signaturpaket: Quellen ändern, `[signatures] version` erhöhen, neu bauen, nur `conf/odinguard/odinguard.sigpack`
  tauschen und den Map-Server neu starten; der Server lehnt ältere Versionen und ungültige Signaturen ab.
- Guard/Core: neues Release bauen, Server und Patcher gemeinsam aktualisieren (Protokoll-Inkompatibilität meldet das
  Studio; v1-Clients sind mit v2-Servern nicht kompatibel).
- Studio: Tab „Updates“ (Kanal stable/beta), siehe `docs/02-architecture.md` §10.
```

`docs/04-reverse-engineering.md`:

```md
# 04 – Reverse engineering of our client (alpha.exe 2018-06-20)

Tools: Ghidra 12.2 (brew, headless) and REA 6.10 (CLI + MCP for Copilot/VS Code, provider Ghidra).
Project: `analysis/_bin/ghidra/ro.gpr` (git-ignored). Scripts: `tools/ghidra/OgSurvey.java`
(callers of imports and string references), `OgDecompile.java`, `OgCallers.java`.

```
export JAVA_HOME=/opt/homebrew/opt/openjdk@25/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home
$(brew --prefix ghidra)/libexec/support/analyzeHeadless analysis/_bin/ghidra ro -process alpha.exe \
  -noanalysis -readOnly -scriptPath tools/ghidra -postScript OgDecompile.java 0097fa40
```

Addresses are for this exe build only (image base 0x400000).

## Network

| Address | Function | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `0x00980030` | winsock init | `WSAStartup`, `LoadLibrary("ws2_32.dll")`, `GetProcAddress` of `send`/`recv` into `DAT_010a33e4` / `DAT_010a33e8` ("Module Hooking Error" message boxes if missing) |
| `0x0097f410` | anti-hook check | compares `GetProcAddress` of connect, closesocket, send, select from a second `LoadLibrary` handle; inline hooks inside ws2_32 pass it |
| `0x0097fa40` | `CConnection::Recv` | `select(read, timeout 0)`, then `recv(…, 0x800)`; `WSAEWOULDBLOCK`/`WSAENOTCONN` = no data |
| `0x0097fb60`, `0x0097feb0` | `CConnection::Send` / flush | `select(write)`, then `send` of the pending buffer slice |

Consequence: OdinGuard hooks `connect`, `send`, `recv`, `select`, `closesocket` inside ws2_32
(MinHook). `select` must report sockets with buffered decrypted data as readable.
`alpha.exe` has no static ws2_32 import; it resolves the functions at runtime.

## Main loop and frame cap

| Address | Function | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `0x009f94e0` | `CModeMgr::Run` | `while running: mode->OnRun(); Sleep(1);` – the frame cap |
| `0x0082e5f0` | precise sleep | only used by the Bink intro video loop (`0x0082e790`) |

`!vsync off` skips `Sleep(1)` on the main thread (the thread that loads the DLL). Verified in the real
client: 1859 skipped waits in about 15 s.

## Chat

The 2018 client prefixes every chat text with a colour code (`|00!ping`). The server strips `|XX`
before it looks for `!` commands.

## Loader

`ijl15.dll` is a static import of `alpha.exe` (WARP rebuilt import table, one descriptor per
function). The OdinGuard loader takes its name and forwards the six exports to `ijl15r.dll`
(ROExt, the previous `ijl15.dll`), which forwards to `ijl15x.dll`.

## Packing

`alpha.exe` is packed: its code section is unpacked only after the static imports (`ijl15.dll`) and their
DLLs have run `DllMain`. Hooks into exe code are therefore installed from a thread that polls up to 60 s
until the expected bytes appear, and every hook checks a byte signature first (`client/src/og_ui.c`).
A different exe build simply leaves the hook inactive ("ui hooks: 0 of 1 active" in `odinguard.log`).

## Text drawing (colour nicks and colour items)

| Address | Function | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `0x006fd780` | `UIWindow::TextOutWithOutline` | `thiscall`, `ret 0x24`: x, y, text, len, fg colour, outline colour, font, height, bold. Draws the name above characters and the names in windows. Signature `55 8B EC 6A FF 68 98 92 B8 00 64 A1 00 00 00 00 50 83 EC 24 53 56 57`. |
| `0x00cf828c` | `UINameBalloonText` vtable | slot 17 = `0x0058a3c0` draws the balloon; colours at `this+0x90` (text) and `+0x94` |
| `0x0042d6d0` | `TextOutW` wrapper | plain GDI text (chat, item windows, status window) |
| `0x0042cc40` | `SetTextColor` wrapper | |

OdinGuard hooks `TextOutWithOutline` (names with outline) and GDI `TextOutW` in gdi32 (all other texts).
Both look the text up in a hash table that the server fills (`OG_S_COLORS`). Item names are matched
without refine (`+7 `), slots (` [4]`) and amounts (`: 5 ea`); character names up to ` (` (guild/party
suffix). `TextLog=1` in `odinguard.ini` logs every drawn text to find the exact form of a new text.

## Hat effects (auras)

The client draws hat effect ids from `data\luafiles514\lua files\hateffectinfo\hateffectinfo.lub`
(the first GRF in DATA.INI wins; ours comes from `core.grf`). An entry is either a `.str` file under
`data\texture\effect\` or a client effect id built into the exe (`hatEffectID`). Missing files show
"Cannot find File" and can crash the client at login, so the server only allows ids from its `og_aura`
list; `check_auras.py` (now part of the separate rAthena aura feature) checks every `.str` entry and its textures. Results for our client
in `05-tests.md`.

## Ground skills (LGP)

No client hook is needed: the map-server sends players with `@lgp` an existing flat ground unit
(Volcano 0x9a, Deluge 0x9b, Violent Gale 0x9c, Land Protector 0x9d) instead of `UNT_DUMMYSKILL` for the
cells of Storm Gust, Meteor Storm, Lord of Vermilion, Heaven's Drive and the Ninja ground skills, and
leaves out the heavy `ZC_NOTIFY_GROUNDSKILL` animation. The textures are in every data.grf, so there are
no missing-file or BMP errors.
```
