## 5. Challenges und Signaturklassen

| Element | Soll | Fehlerfälle | Ergebnis |
|---|---|---|---|
| ch-nonce | gültiger Digest mit Build-Secret | falsches Secret → Fehlschlag; Replay → `challenge:replay`; Timeout | grün (E2E 8, 26) |
| ch-code | Bereich des kanonischen Images stimmt | gepatchter Code → Fehlschlag | grün (ehrlicher Client E2E 8; Patch-Fall über Heartbeat-Hash E2E 40/41) |
| ch-time | Uhr-Drift ≤ `max_drift_percent` | Speedhack | grün (E2E 8, 26, 39) |
| ch-file | Bereich von `odin.grf`/Pack stimmt | Pflichtdatei fehlt/anders → Fehlschlag; optional fehlt → ok | grün (E2E 27–29) |
| ch-honeypot | nur Bots treffen den Lockvogel | Treffer → flagban | grün (E2E 17) |
| ch-captcha | Captcha nach Verhaltens-Flags, nie WoE/BG | falsche Antwort/Timeout | Server-Logik gebaut, Spiel-UI: Abnahme A9 |
| behaviour nodelay | Skill innerhalb Delay → Flag | – | grün (E2E 18) |
| rate-limit | > pps → Aktion | Warnmodus = Log | grün (E2E 19) |
| Signaturen process/module/window_class/window_title/file_name | Treffer gemeldet, einmal pro Verbindung | Allowlist unterdrückt | grün (`dettest`) |
| file_sha256 / grf_sha256 | Hash-Treffer | Allowlist-Hash unterdrückt | grün (`dettest`, synthetische Fixtures) |
| driver | Treiber/Dienst-Name | – | grün (`dettest`: aktiver Systemtreiber als synthetische Signatur) |
| mutex / registry | benannte Objekte, Registry-Schlüssel | fehlender Schlüssel → kein Treffer | grün (`dettest`) |
| GRF-Manifest | Tabellen-Hash, Voll-Hash, Mods, Pflicht | Patch-Rollout mit mehreren Versionen | grün (E2E 32–37, Unit `grf::*`) |
| grf_entry / import_pattern / string_pattern | nur Analyse, nicht client-prüfbar | – | dokumentiert (Paket überspringt sie, `sigpack::build_verify_cap_and_skip`) |
| Fehlalarme legitimer Client | ROExt, dxwrapper, Skins ohne Treffer | – | grün (`dettest clean`) |
| Signaturpaket | nur mit gültiger Signatur + Mindestversion | manipuliert/fremd → abgelehnt | grün (Unit + E2E 25) |

| A6 | `@lgp`, `@square 2`, `@circle`, `@aoes` mit Storm Gust, LoV, Meteor Storm | flache blaue/orange Zellen pro Zelle, Charaktere sichtbar; Vergleich mit darkworld-Boden (Kontrast) |
| A7 | Competitive-Pack (Standard: Flachmaps WoE/BG/PvP, dunkle Böden, Bäume, Pneuma) | Ladereihenfolge `0=odin.grf`, `1=odin-dark.grf`; flache WoE-/BG-Maps mit dunklen Kacheln, Pneuma-Countdown; FPS/Ladezeit notieren; keine `grf:*`-Meldung |
| A7b | GRF-Prüfung mit echtem Client | Dev-Client ohne Änderung: keine Meldung; darkworld `dark.grf` zusätzlich: keine Meldung (erlaubter Mod); geänderte data.grf: `grf:modified` |
| A8 | Challenges einschalten (Stufe 1, je eins): nonce, code, time, file | keine Fehlschläge für ehrliche Spieler über 24 h |
| A9 | Verhalten + Captcha auf einem Testaccount mit Makro-Muster | Captcha erscheint, nicht auf WoE/BG-Maps |
| A10 | Input-Filter, RCX, Warsaw, VM-Block auf VMware/VirtualBox/Hyper-V | echte Rechner: Verhalten wie konfiguriert, keine Abstürze |
| A11 | Rollout-Gate: `og rollout` mit Export aus Stufe 1 | Fehlalarm-Kandidaten geprüft, dann Stufe 2 |
| A12 | Studio auf Windows/Linux bauen (`release_studio.sh`) | signiertes Artefakt, `og update-verify` ok |

## 7. Offene Testlücken (ehrlich)

- Wiedergespielter Record als eigener E2E-Fall; Ratenlimit pro Command.
- Echte Cheat-Programme wurden nicht ausgeführt (nur statische Analyse und harmlose Stubs); Treffer echter Tools
  bestätigt erst die Abnahme auf einem Testrechner.
- Input-Filter: Parallels verwirft synthetische Eingaben schon vor dem Gast (v0.3-Befund), daher nur auf echter
  Hardware.
- Questlog-Texte, Captcha-Fenster, LGP-Look: nur im echten Client.
- CFG nur mit llvm-mingw (`TOOLCHAIN=llvm`); der Standard-Build (mingw-gcc) hat es nicht. Visual-Studio-Builds des
  Server-Patches sind ungetestet.

## 8. Historie

Die Ergebnisse von v0.1–v0.3 (Handshake, Hardware-Bans, Rechner-Limit, Alive-Timeout, Farb-Nicks, Auren-IDs,
Release-Paket) gelten weiter für den unveränderten Code; Details im Git-Verlauf dieser Datei (Commit `4ad6498`).

# 06 – OdinGuard compared with Gepard Shield 3.0

> **Stand 1.0.0 (2026-11-23):** Die Matrix unten stammt aus v0.3 und gilt weiter. Neu in 1.0 (Details

> weder Modulauswahl durch den Betreiber noch offene, signierte Signaturpakete [gelesen: öffentliche Featureliste].
> Datei-Integrität läuft jetzt über `ch-file`/`og verify-release` statt `tools/make_manifest.py` (entfernt).

State: OdinGuard v0.3.0 (2026-11-23). "Tested" means tested end to end with our 2018-06-20 client and
xAthena (`05-tests.md`). Gepard facts are from its public feature list; its code was not used.

## Feature matrix

| Gepard 3.0 feature | OdinGuard | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Exe code integrity in memory | SHA-256 of the unpacked code section, sent in every heartbeat; server compares with `og_allowed_exe` | tested; **better**: checked continuously, not only at start |
| File integrity exe + DLLs | file hashes in the report, `tools/make_manifest.py` | built; server list optional |
| DLL injection protection | module scan + report of unknown modules, action per server rule | tested (report) |
| Dynamic packet encryption | X25519 per connection, server key pinned (Ed25519), XChaCha20-Poly1305 for the **whole** game stream | tested; **better**: authenticated encryption, replayed or changed bytes are rejected |
| Packet editors / sniffers / bots (WPE, RPE, OpenKore) | encrypted stream + signed heartbeat; tools from the signature list kick or ban | tested (OpenKore signature, plain clients refused when `og_required`) |
| Malformed chat packets | server strips colour codes and checks commands; xAthena validates lengths | server side |
| Unique ID, ban by ID | 13 hardware components (MachineGuid, SMBIOS, disks, volume, CPU, MAC, ...), salted; exact **and fuzzy** ban (k of n) | tested; **better**: a changed MAC or disk does not lift the ban |
| Max windows per machine | client semaphore + server limit per machine (`og_max_per_machine`) | tested; **better**: also enforced by the server |
| Block VMs | CPUID + firmware strings, policy from the server | built; Parallels detected, other hypervisors untested |
| Known cheat tools (PotND, meth4u, xRag, xLike, RoTools, ...) | process / window / module signatures **delivered by the server** | tested; **better**: new tools without a client update |
| 2018 client, 2010+ clients | loader proxy without exe patch, exe hooks with byte signatures (inactive on other builds) | tested with 2018-06-20 |
| RCX final | loads after RCX through the same proxy chain, RCX modules tolerated | **untested** (needs a machine with RCX) |
| Warsaw (Brazil) | hooks only ws2_32 / gdi32 / exe code, tolerates foreign modules | **untested** (needs a Warsaw machine) |
| Crash log (stack, GRFs, resources, last packets) | registers, stack walk, stack dump, modules, GRF list, last 32 packets | tested |
| `!vsync`, `!crash`, `!ping` | same commands | tested |
| Automatic SQL tables + config | `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS`, config with defaults | tested |
| Synthetic input block | low-level hooks reject injected mouse/keyboard events | built, **untested** (Parallels drops synthetic input) |
| Nodelay / animation delay | server-side `min_skill_delay_limit` + exe code hash | tested (hash) |
| GRF override protection | resource rules (loose files, GRF order), action per server rule | tested (report) |
| LGP | server-side: flat ground units per viewer (`@lgp`) | tested; **better**: no client files, no BMP errors, works for every client with OdinGuard |
| Custom auras | hat effects, allow list `og_aura`, `@aura` | tested; resource check tool |
| Colour nicks | server colour list, drawn by the exe text hook | tested |
| Colour items | server colour list per item id | tested |

## Only in OdinGuard

- `@showauras` (hide auras of others per player) and `@lgp` as player commands.
- Alive timeout: a client that stops sending heartbeats is logged or kicked.
- Machine bans with fuzzy matching and `@oginfo` (version, build, machine, exe hash per character).
- Everything configured on the server (signatures, policy, colours, auras, LGP): no client update needed.
- Own key per deployment, open protocol in `proto/og_proto.h`, reproducible builds (same input, same
  DLL hash).
- Auras moved out of OdinGuard in 1.0 into a separate rAthena feature (incl. `check_auras.py`, not part of this repository).

## Still open

- Tests on real machines: input filter, RCX, Warsaw, VM block on VMware/VirtualBox/Hyper-V.
- Exe import patch (guard loaded by the exe itself instead of the `ijl15.dll` proxy) and Authenticode
  signing of the DLLs (reduces antivirus false positives).
- Live rollout steps: `og_log_only: no`, then `og_required: yes` (see `server/README.md`).
- Website list of the player commands.

## Language: C, and why not Rust (yet)

The client is C11 (mingw-w64, 32-bit), the server module C++ inside xAthena. Crypto: Monocypher, hooks:
MinHook.

Rust would work (`i686-pc-windows-gnu` or `-msvc`): memory safety for the parsers (handshake, records,
colour lists), `cargo` for dependencies. But:

- **Speed is not the reason.** The guard does little per frame: a hash table lookup per drawn text and an
  AEAD record per network packet. Both cost microseconds in C; Rust would be the same speed.
- **The risky part stays `unsafe`.** Hooks on exe addresses, `thiscall` trampolines, Win32 callbacks and
  raw packets are FFI either way.
- **Size and build.** A 32-bit Rust DLL with std is larger, and the toolchain for the 2018 client
  (i686, no UCRT surprises) needs extra care.
- **Working, tested code.** v0.3 is tested end to end; a rewrite would mean the same tests again.

Recommendation: stay in C for the client DLL and keep the parsers small (fuzz test: done in 1.0, `make -C client fuzz`).
Decision record for 1.0: `02-architecture.md` §12 (client C, server C++, Studio and tools Rust). Rust is a
good choice for new standalone tools (patcher, manifest/asset tools; RustyGRF already is Rust).

### 1.5 Empfehlung **[Vorschlag]**

1. **Sofort (Estland-/WoE-RO-Look, belegt):** Variante B. `og_lgp` für 89, 83, 85 auf `0x9b`;
   `odin.grf` überschreibt **eine** Datei: `data\texture\effect\ring_blue.tga` (64×64, TGA 32 bit,
   unten 4 Zeilen Blau mit Alpha 230, Rest Alpha 0; Größe wie Original 16 428 B). Ergebnis: alle
   drei Skills als flache blaue Zellquadrate, wie auf WoE-RO/EstlandRO.
2. **Ziel (ohne Deluge-Verwechslung, nach Ingame-Test):** Variante A. SG/LoV/MS → `0xc8`
   (`hanmoon1.tga`, blaue Kachel 128×128 TGA32 mit Rahmen Alpha 210 und Füllung Alpha 70). Für
   Farben je Skill: Meteor → `0xc9` (`hanmoon2.tga`, orange). LoV bleibt blau auf `0xc8` (wie
   Estland) oder später auf eine dritte getestete Unit.
3. Heaven's Drive (91) und NJ 541 von `0x9d` wegnehmen (z. B. `0x9b` bzw. `0xc8`).

Testplan: auf dem Testserver `og_lgp: 89,0xc8` (bzw. `0xc9`) setzen, Map-Server neu starten,
`@lgp` an, Storm Gust wirken; erwartet: pro Zelle eine flache Kachel, keine „Cannot find file“.
Dasselbe mit `odin-lgp-test-primary.grf` bzw. `-fallback.grf` an erster Stelle in `DATA.INI`.

**Zielpfade für odin.grf** (Schreibweise wie im 2018er `data.grf`, reines ASCII, daher keine
cp949-Kodierung nötig; der Client vergleicht case-insensitiv) **[gemessen]**:

| Variante | Pfad im GRF | Datei aus `analysis/_work/lgp/own/` |
|---|---|---|
| B | `data\texture\effect\ring_blue.tga` | `stage_fallback/data/texture/effect/ring_blue.tga` |
| B+ | `data\texture\effect\ring_red.tga`, `data\texture\effect\ring_yellow.tga` | `stage_fallback/…` (rot, violett) |
| A | `data\texture\effect\hanmoon1.tga` | `stage_primary/data/texture/effect/hanmoon1.tga` (blau) |
| A | `data\texture\effect\hanmoon2.tga` | `stage_primary/data/texture/effect/hanmoon2.tga` (orange) |
| (nur Referenz) | `data\texture\effect\aaa copy.bmp` (mit Leerzeichen) | `bmp/lgp128_*_fill.bmp` |

Koreanische Pfade (nicht nötig für LGP) müssen in cp949 stehen, z. B. `이팩트` = `c0 cc c6 d1 c6 ae`,
`유저인터페이스` = `c0 af c0 fa c0 ce c5 cd c6 e4 c0 cc bd ba`; `rgrf build` erhält sie, wenn der
Ordner mit `--names cp949` extrahiert wurde.

## Teil 2 – darkworld-Kategorien (Competitive-Pack)

**Entscheidung des Eigentümers (2026-11-24) [gelesen]:** Alle darkworld-Änderungen dürfen
ausgeliefert werden, wenn der Betreiber sie auswählt – jeder Spieler erhält dasselbe Pack
(`odin-dark.grf`), also einen gleichen Standard wie auf WoE RO / EstlandRO. Das schließt flache
Maps, durchsichtige Bäume/Objekte, verkleinerte WoE-Objekte, den Pneuma-Countdown, nodelay-ACTs und
dunkle Bodenkacheln ein. Lizenz der darkworld-Dateien laut Eigentümer: frei (mit GRF Editor erstellt).
Jede Kategorie ist **einzeln wählbar**; die Befunde unten beschreiben, was eine Kategorie ändert,
damit der Betreiber bewusst wählt.

### 2.1 Diff-Statistik **[gemessen]**

Groß/Klein-Unterschied): dark 2552 geändert / 736 neu / 28 gleich; dark2 2871 / 785 / 33;

### 2.2 Maps

schg_cas01) **[gemessen]**. Optik: dunkelgrün = begehbar, schwarz = blockiert, beige = snipable,
dunkelblau = Wasser; WoE-SE-Burgen zusätzlich Markierungen (`points\*`, `woe\*`: Pfeile „UPPER STAGE“,
Ziffern, farbige Felder an Geräte-/Barrikadenpositionen).

spätere Ordner überschreiben).

### 2.5 Flache Maps aus RustyGRF statt aus darkworld **[gemessen]**

`rgrf map flat --flatten --remove-light --remove-shadow <Client-Ordner> [Maps]` liest die Maps über
die DATA.INI des Clients (das Skript legt dafür eine DATA.INI ohne `odin*.grf` an) und schreibt nur
die geänderten `.rsw/.gnd/.gat`. Damit ist das Ergebnis für jeden Client reproduzierbar. Vergleich mit
dark2 für die 72 WoE/BG/PvP-Maps, die beide haben (`analysis/_work/competitive/cmp_flat.json`):

| Merkmal | RustyGRF flat | darkworld dark2 |
|---|---|---|
| Modelle/Lichter/Sounds/Effekte in `.rsw` | 0 (72/72) | 0 (72/72) |
| Wasserhöhe | 100 (unter dem Boden) | 100 |
| Höhen GND/GAT | 0 (72/72) | 0 (72/72) |
| Wandflächen | 0 | 0 |
| Lightmaps | 1 | 1 |
| GAT-Zelltypen | = Client | 69/72 gleich; aldeg_cas01 (129 Zellen), te_prt_gld (88), arug_cas03 (2) weichen ab |
| Bodentexturen | Originaltexturen, leere Zellen bleiben leer (z. B. prtg_cas01 4291 von 12 100 Zellen mit Boden) | jede Zelle eine Kachel `c*.bmp` (12 100 / 12 100) |

Die Kachel-Optik von darkworld entsteht in OdinGuard durch `competitive.py floor --fill-void` auf den
RustyGRF-Flachmaps (Kachelname aus den 4 GAT-Zellen, Kachel-UV wie in dark, WoE-Markierungen
`points\*`/`woe\*` aus der dark2-GND übernommen, wo die 4 GAT-Zellen gleich sind: 31 339 Zellen,
fast nur SE-Burgen arug/schg_cas*). GND 1.8/1.9 (124 neuere Maps) werden mit unverändertem Wasserteil
geschrieben; Lesen→Schreiben ist für alle 1028 Flach-GNDs bytegleich. `1@exsr` bleibt ohne Kacheln
(seine `.gat` ändert `map flat` nicht und schreibt sie daher nicht ins Flach-Archiv).

Der frühere Kandidat `analysis/_work/dark/odin-dark-candidate.grf` (59 Maps, 23 MB) ist durch den
Ordner `floor` ersetzt (68 Bodendateien, gleiche Methode, zusätzlich rush/bat_c-Grounds,
UV der Kachel jetzt immer ganz statt teils aus der Original-Fläche).

### 2.6 Ladereihenfolge, Pfade, Kodierung **[gemessen]**

`DATA.INI`: `0=odin.grf`, `1=odin-dark.grf`, danach die GRFs des Clients (Dev-Client: cdata, core,
cpal, data). Prüfung aller Staging-Pfade gegen den Dev-Client (`analysis/_work/competitive/conflicts.json`):

* **odin.grf vor odin-dark.grf:** `effects` enthält `texture\effect\hanmoon1.tga`/`hanmoon2.tga`
  (darkworld: 1×1 Magenta), die auch odin.grf (LGP-Kacheln) hat – odin.grf gewinnt, die LGP bleibt.
  Sonst keine Überschneidung mit odin.grf (`data\odinguard\profile.txt`, hanmoon1/2).
* **odin-dark.grf vor den Client-GRFs:** überschreibt auch Dateien aus `cdata.grf` (effects 8, other
  11, flat-maps-all 21) und `cpal.grf` (nodelay: 49 von 56 Körper-Sprites kommen im Dev-Client aus
  cpal.grf; die nodelay-Sprites ersetzen sie – eigene Färbungen/Paletten prüfen **[vermutet]**).
* **Groß/Klein:** 22 Pfade unterscheiden sich vom data.grf-Eintrag nur in der Schreibweise
  (trees 19, z. B. `JA_FF1.bmp`; ui 1 `prt_sewB1.bmp`; flat-maps-all 2 `Tha_t05.gat/.gnd`). Der Client
  vergleicht ohne Groß/Klein **[gelesen, Teil 1]**; `rgrf build` lehnt Kollisionen ab, im Pack gibt es
  keine. Alle Zielpfade sind klein geschrieben (Staging auf macOS ist case-insensitiv).
* **Kodierung:** alle Namen sind cp949-darstellbar; extrahiert mit `--names cp949`, gebaut mit
  `--names cp949`. Die Rohbytes stimmen mit data.grf überein (z. B. `몬스터` = `b8 f3 bd ba c5 cd`,
  verglichen mit `rgrf --names raw ls`).
* **Zwischen Kategorien:** Überschneidungen nur bei den Map-Varianten (gewollt, s. Kombinationsregel)
  und den Kachel-Texturen (identische Dateien).

### 2.7 Was RustyGRF (noch) nicht kann **[gemessen]**

* `map flat` hat keine Option für GRF Editors Kachel-Texturen (GAT-codierte `c*.bmp`, „custom
  textures“); deshalb setzt `tools/pack/competitive.py floor` die Kacheln auf die GND (Python).
* Kein Befehl, um GND-Flächen neu zu texturieren oder leere Zellen zu füllen (dasselbe).
* `map info` zeigt bei GND keine Zahl der Lightmaps, Flächen, Wände und Höhen; der Vergleich lief über
  einen eigenen Parser.
* „Simplify maps“ (Modelle teilweise behalten, wie Thoth) gibt es nur als Ganz-oder-gar-nicht
  (`--remove-models`/`--remove-objects`), keine Auswahl einzelner Modelle.
* `extract` nimmt nur ein Muster (keine Liste/Manifest-Datei), `ls`-Muster kennen keine
  Zeichenklassen (`[an]`); `-q` unterdrückt die Zusammenfassung von `extract` nicht.
* Kein Bild-/Sprite-Vergleich (Transparenz-Anteil, Größe gegenüber Vanilla) als Befehl; Werte für
  `trees` stammen aus der früheren Pillow-Messung.
* `map flat` endet mit Code 3, wenn Maps des Clients Dateien fehlen (air_evt, soccer3), obwohl das
  Archiv geschrieben ist; das Skript wertet 3 als Erfolg.

### 2.8 Offene Punkte

* Ingame-Test, ob 0xc8/0xc9 im 2018er Client flach pro Zelle gezeichnet werden (Variante A).
* Ob die Original-Geometrie von Volcano/Deluge/VG vier Seiten (Quadrat) oder rund ist; bestimmt, ob
  Variante B Quadrate oder Ringe zeigt (WoE-RO-Spieler sahen Quadrate).
* Ob die `cps.dll` des Clients LZMA kann (sonst zlib/zopfli).
* Ingame-Test der Kategorien im 2018er Client: Optik `floor`/`floor-flat-*`, nodelay mit den
  cpal.grf-Sprites, Kamera-Tabellen aus `other`.
* Studio: `recipe.toml` lesen (Standard, Varianten, Kombinationsregel) statt der freien Ordnerliste.

## Reproduktion

Skripte unter `analysis/_work/{lgp,dark}/tools/`: `strinfo.py` (STR), `imgstat.py`, `sheet.py`
(Kontaktbögen), `idx.py`/`cat.py` (Hash-Index, Gruppen), `rofmt.py` (GAT/GND/RSW), `texstats.py`,
`sprcmp.py`, `gatall.py`, `classify.py`, `build_fair_gnd.py`, `make_tiles.py`. Die großen
Zwischendaten (Hash-JSON der Vanilla-GRFs, extrahierte Maps) wurden gelöscht; neu erzeugen mit
`rgrf --names cp949 --json hash <grf>` und `rgrf --names cp949 extract <grf> maps/<quelle> 'data\<map>.gnd'`.

Competitive-Pack: `DARK_DIR=<Ordner mit dark.grf, dark2.grf, nodelay.grf> CLIENT_DIR=<Client mit DATA.INI>
tools/pack/build_categories.sh [ordner …]` (rgrf + Python 3.9, idempotent; zweiter Lauf bytegleich
geprüft; `TEST_GRF_DIR=…` baut und prüft je Ordner eine Test-GRF). Klassifikation und Prüfungen:
`analysis/_work/competitive/tools/{classify.py,cmp_flat.py,conflicts.py}`.

`docs/INTEGRATION.md`:

```md
# Integrating OdinGuard Anti Cheat into your server and client

This guide takes a server owner from zero to a protected rAthena server: build a release from a profile, patch
the server, ship the client files, configure the GRF check for your patcher, and roll out in stages without
locking out honest players.

German notes: [03-integration.md](03-integration.md). Architecture: [02-architecture.md](02-architecture.md).

## 0. What you need

| | |
|---|---|
| Server | rAthena (or a fork) with MariaDB/MySQL, C++17 toolchain. Tested: PACKETVER 20180620 pre-renewal. |
| Client | Windows client 2010-07-30 or newer that loads `ijl15.dll` (all Ragexe/RagexeRE builds do). Tested: 2018-06-20. |
| Build machine | macOS or Linux with `mingw-w64` (`brew install mingw-w64` / `apt install mingw-w64`), Rust (rustup), optional Node.js for the Studio GUI. Windows works through WSL. |
| Patcher | any patcher that can ship files and DATA.INI changes (Thor, NeonCube, rpatchur, ...). |

## 1. Build the Studio and create a profile

```sh
git clone https://github.com/kxdrsrt/OdinGuard && cd OdinGuard
cd studio && cargo build --release && cd ..
export PATH="$PWD/studio/target/release:$PATH"      # the `og` command

og new myserver.profile.toml --id myserver --operator "My Ragnarok"
```

`og new` writes the profile and three secret files next to it (`keys/server.seed`, `keys/signing.seed`,
`keys/build.secret`). **Back them up and never commit or ship them.** If you lose `server.seed`, every client you
shipped must be replaced; if you change `general.hwid_salt`, every machine ban becomes useless.

The GUI does the same with forms: `cd studio/apps/studio && npm install && npx tauri dev`.

## 2. Choose modules, commands and signatures

Open the profile in the Studio (tab *Module & Challenges*) or edit the TOML:

- `modules` – what is built into the DLL and enabled on the server. Unselected modules are not compiled into the
  client (the build checks the linker map). Start with the default set; challenges, `rate-limit`, `behaviour`,
  `ch-captcha`, `ch-honeypot` are opt-in.
- `[params]` – module parameters (`"heartbeat.interval" = 30`, `"multi-client.max_per_machine" = 3`, ...). The
  Studio shows ranges and refuses invalid values (`og validate`).
- `[commands.<id>]` – switch commands off, rename them, change the minimum group or the rate limit.
- `[signatures]` – signature sources and allowlists (`signatures/*.toml`), `max_action` (caps every signature
  action, e.g. `flagban` during the rollout) and per tool group: `[signatures.groups] RCX = "kick"`,
  `GRF = "off"`, `DEBUG = "log"`. `og sig-groups myserver.profile.toml` lists the groups.

Add your own signatures in a separate TOML file (same format as `signatures/signatures.toml`) and list it in
`signatures.sources`. Legitimate tools your players use go to an allowlist file (`[[allow]]`, kinds `file_sha256`,
`grf_sha256`, `path`).

## 3. GRF check (Gepard-style, patcher friendly)

The guard compares every GRF in the client's `DATA.INI` with your list: name, size and a *tail hash* (header +
file table, checked at every scan in milliseconds), and in a background thread the full-file SHA-256.

```sh
og grf-scan myserver.profile.toml --client /path/to/your/clean/client --full
og grf-allow myserver.profile.toml /path/to/dark.grf --note "darkworld"     # optional mods, any name
```

- `grf.file` – accepted versions of your GRFs. Several versions with the same name may be listed.
- `grf.mod` – GRFs players may add (skins, translations, darkworld variants), matched by content, not by name.
- `grf.overlays` – folders where loose files are allowed (e.g. `data\texture\skin\`).
- Actions: `modified_action` (default `kick`), `unknown_action` (`log`), `missing_action` (`log`).
- `odin.grf` and the competitive pack are added by every build automatically.

**Patching workflow** (no false alarms while players update):

1. Build your patch and apply it to a clean client copy.
2. `og grf-scan myserver.profile.toml --client <patched copy> --full --keep-previous` (old and new versions are both
   accepted now).
3. `og build`, deploy the new server config (only `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt` changes), restart the map-server.
4. Publish the patch through your patcher.
5. After a few days run `og grf-scan` without `--keep-previous` to drop the old versions.

## 4. Optional: competitive pack

An optional GRF (`odin-dark.grf`) that every player gets from you, so everyone plays with the same visuals (dark
floors, flat maps, simplified effects, ... – WoE RO / darkworld style). Pick categories in the Studio tab
*Competitive-Pack* (recipe `assets/competitive/recipe.toml`, staging folders built by
`tools/pack/build_categories.sh`) or point `assets.competitive_pack` to a ready GRF. Its hash enters the GRF
check, so modified or foreign variants are reported.

## 5. Build and verify the release

```sh
og build myserver.profile.toml          # -> output folder of the profile
og verify-release dist/myserver         # signature of manifest.json and every file hash
```

| Folder | Content | Goes to |
|---|---|---|
| `client/` | `odinguard.dll`, `ijl15.dll` (loader), `odin.grf`, `[odin-dark.grf]`, `odinguard.ini`, `README.txt`, licences | your patcher |
| `server/` | module sources, `conf/odinguard_athena.conf`, `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt`, `conf/odinguard/` (signature package, reference DLL and GRFs), SQL | your rAthena |
| `secrets/odinguard.env` | `ODINGUARD_KEY`, `ODINGUARD_PROTO_SALT`, `ODINGUARD_BUILD_SECRET` | server environment only |
| `patcher/filelist.txt` | file, SHA-256, size | your patcher's file list |
| `docs/` | operator handbook, command reference (de/en), build report | you |

Builds are reproducible: the same profile and sources give byte-identical files. For Control Flow Guard build the
client with llvm-mingw: `OG_TOOLCHAIN=llvm og build ...` (see `client/Makefile`, `LLVM_MINGW`).

## 6. Server (rAthena)

**Quick path (upstream rAthena):** apply `server/patches/rathena-4cd08b7.patch` in your rAthena checkout
(`git apply --check …` then `git apply …`). It contains steps 1–4 below (module files, Monocypher, all hooks, Makefile,
CMake and Visual Studio entries, `conf/odinguard_athena.conf`). Run `./configure` again, rebuild and continue with
step 5. Base commit, conflict resolution on newer rAthena and PACKETVER notes: [`server/patches/README.md`](../server/patches/README.md).

**Manual steps** (forks, or when the patch does not apply):

1. Copy `server/src/common/*`, `server/src/login/*`, `server/src/map/*` into the same folders of rAthena.
   `og_crypto.cpp` compiles Monocypher: copy `third_party/monocypher.c/.h` to `3rdparty/monocypher/`.
2. Add the hook lines listed in [`server/HOOKS.txt`](../server/HOOKS.txt) (socket layer, login, char and map
   server, atcommands, `conf/groups.yml`). [`server/README.md`](../server/README.md) explains each hook.
3. Add `odinguard.o og_crypto.o og_wire.o` to `src/common/Makefile.in` (and the CMake list), add `og_wire.c`,
   `og_wire.h`, `og_proto.h` to the common header dependencies, run `./configure` again and rebuild.
4. Copy `server/conf/*` into `conf/` (keeps your edits out of `odinguard_athena.conf`: the generated
   `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt` overrides it).
5. Put the three values of `secrets/odinguard.env` into the server environment (Docker/Easypanel/systemd), or as
   `og_key`, `og_proto_salt`, `og_build_secret` lines into `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt` (keep that file out of
   git then).
6. Start the servers. Tables (`og_client`, `og_component`, `og_ban`, `og_event`, `og_flag`) are created
   automatically; the map-server log shows `OdinGuard Anti Cheat: enabled (...)`.

## 7. Client

1. In the client folder rename the existing `ijl15.dll` (e.g. ROExt's proxy) to `ijl15r.dll`. A plain client has
   Intel's `ijl15.dll`: rename that to `ijl15r.dll` too.
2. Ship `client/ijl15.dll` and `client/odinguard.dll` next to the exe. Load chain:
   `exe → ijl15.dll (OdinGuard loader) → ijl15r.dll (ROExt or Intel) [→ ijl15x.dll]`; the loader also starts the
   guard.
3. Put `odin.grf` (and `odin-dark.grf`) first in `DATA.INI`:
   ```ini
   [Data]
   0=odin.grf
   1=odin-dark.grf
   2=rdata.grf
   3=data.grf
   ```
4. Add every file of `client/` plus `ijl15r.dll` and `DATA.INI` to your patcher's required list.
5. Players never install or uninstall anything themselves; there is no player uninstaller.

## 8. Roll out in stages

| Stage | Server | Effect | Move on when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 warn | `og_required: no`, `og_log_only: yes` | everything is only logged; flags collect, the ban wave runs dry | `og rollout` shows no unreviewed rule above the false-alarm threshold |
| 2 kick | `og_log_only: no` | actions apply to clients with the guard; players without it still play | false alarms stay low |
| 3 patcher | as 2 | the guard reaches every player | most active accounts log in with the guard |
| 4 required | `og_required: yes` | no login without a valid guard of your build | – |

The stage is a profile setting (`[rollout] stage`). Export `og_event` and `og_client` (`mysql -B -e "SELECT ..."`)
and run `og rollout myserver.profile.toml --events og_event.tsv --clients og_client.tsv --advance`, then rebuild
and deploy the server config. The Studio tab *Rollout* does the same.

## 9. Day-to-day

- In game: `@oginfo <name>` (guard version, machine, exe hash), `@ogflags [name]` (open flags), `@ogbanwave dry`
  (who the next ban wave would ban), `@ogban <name>, <reason>`, `@ogunban <account id>`.
- New signatures: edit your signature TOML, raise `signatures.version`, rebuild, replace
  `conf/odinguard/odinguard.sigpack`, restart the map-server. No client update needed.
- New OdinGuard version: rebuild with the same profile and keys, deploy server and client together (the Studio
  warns about protocol changes).

## 10. Troubleshooting

| Symptom | Cause / fix |
|---|---|
| Map log: `signature package signature INVALID` | package built with another signing key, or edited: rebuild and copy `conf/odinguard/` again |
| Client message "client built for another server" | the DLL was built from another profile (status 3) |
| Everyone gets `grf:modified` after a patch | the new GRF versions were not scanned before the patch – section 3 |
| `grf:unknown` for a skin GRF | allow it with `og grf-allow` or set `grf.unknown_action = "log"` |
| Antivirus warns about `odinguard.dll` | sign the DLLs with your Authenticode certificate; submit the files to the vendor |
| Detection of a legitimate tool | add it to an allowlist file, or set its group to `log` in `signatures.groups` |

`proto/og_proto.h`:

```h
/* OdinGuard Anti Cheat – wire protocol v2. Shared by the client DLL (C) and the server module (C++).
 * All integers little-endian. The parsers for every message live in og_wire.c (pure C, fuzzed natively).
 *
 * 1. Client hello (plaintext, first bytes on every game TCP connection):
 *      u16 id = OG_HELLO_ID ("OG"), u16 len, u8 version, u8 flags,
 *      u8 eph_pub[32], u8 nonce[32], u8 unique_id[32], u8 exe_code[32], char build[16], u8 profile_tag[16],
 *      u8 n, n x { char name[16]; u8 hash[32]; }
 *    profile_tag = BLAKE2b-128("OdinGuard/tag" || proto_salt): a client built for another server is refused
 *    with a clear message instead of failing on the first record.
 * 2. Server hello (plaintext):
 *      u16 id = OG_HELLO_ID, u16 len, u8 version, u8 status,
 *      u8 eph_pub[32], u8 nonce[32], u8 sig[64], char message[]
 *    sig = EdDSA(server static key, BLAKE2b-512(client hello || server hello without sig and message)).
 *    The signed transcript contains both version bytes: a downgrade is detected by both sides.
 * 3. Keys: BLAKE2b-512("OdinGuard/v2" || proto_salt || X25519(eph) || client_pub || server_pub || nonce_c || nonce_s)
 *      first 32 bytes = client->server key, last 32 = server->client key
 * 4. Records (both directions after the hellos):
 *      u16 body_len, u8 mac[16], u8 body[body_len]
 *      body = AEAD(XChaCha20-Poly1305, key, nonce = u64 counter || 16 zero bytes, ad = the 2 length bytes)
 *      plaintext body = u8 type, payload. type 0 = game stream bytes, type 1 = control message.
 *    Key rotation: before the record with counter c (c > 0, c % OG_REKEY_RECORDS == 0) the direction key becomes
 *    BLAKE2b-256(key || "OdinGuard/rekey"); the old key is wiped (forward secrecy inside a session).
 *    Replay: the counter is implicit, a replayed, dropped or reordered record fails authentication.
 */
#ifndef OG_PROTO_H
#define OG_PROTO_H

#define OG_HELLO_ID        0x474F /* bytes "OG" */
#define OG_PROTO_VERSION   2
#define OG_PROTO_MIN       2      /* lowest version a v2 peer accepts (downgrade protection) */
#define OG_HELLO_MAX       2048
#define OG_COMPONENT_NAME  16
#define OG_MAX_COMPONENTS  24
#define OG_RECORD_MAX      60000  /* plaintext payload per record */
#define OG_RECORD_OVERHEAD (2 + 16 + 1)
#define OG_REKEY_RECORDS   4096
#define OG_TAG_LEN         16
#define OG_SALT_LEN        16

#define OG_CLIENT_HELLO_FIXED (2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 32 + 32 + 32 + 32 + 16 + OG_TAG_LEN + 1)
#define OG_SERVER_HELLO_FIXED (2 + 2 + 1 + 1 + 32 + 32 + 64)

/* client hello flags */
#define OG_FLAG_VM        0x01
#define OG_FLAG_DEBUGGER  0x02

/* server hello status */
#define OG_STATUS_OK       0
#define OG_STATUS_OUTDATED 1
#define OG_STATUS_REFUSED  2
#define OG_STATUS_PROFILE  3 /* client built for another server (profile tag) */

/* record types */
#define OG_REC_GAME    0
#define OG_REC_CONTROL 1

/* control messages, client -> server */
#define OG_C_ALIVE    0x01 /* u32 seq, u8 exe_code[32], u16 unknown_modules, u8 flags (OG_ALIVE_*), u8 guard_code[32] */
#define OG_C_DETECT   0x02 /* u16 signature_id, u8 kind, char text[] */
#define OG_C_PONG     0x03 /* u32 server_tick */
#define OG_C_REPORT   0x04 /* char text[]: answer to a command, shown to the player */
#define OG_C_RESPONSE 0x05 /* u32 challenge_id, u8 type, u8 status (OG_CH_ST_*), u8 digest[32], u32 a, u32 b */

#define OG_ALIVE_LEN            (1 + 4 + 32 + 2 + 1 + 32)
#define OG_ALIVE_HOOKS_TAMPERED 0x01
#define OG_ALIVE_DEBUGGER       0x02
#define OG_ALIVE_GRF_VIOLATION  0x04
#define OG_ALIVE_API_HOOKED     0x08 /* timing/input APIs patched by a foreign module (speed hacks, macro tools) */
#define OG_ALIVE_HW_BREAKPOINT  0x10 /* debug registers set on the game thread */

/* control messages, server -> client */
#define OG_S_POLICY    0x81 /* u8 block_vm, u8 max_windows, u16 alive_interval_s, u8 input_filter, u8 grf_strict,
                               u16 n (always 0 in v2, signatures come with OG_S_SIGS) */
#define OG_S_PING      0x82 /* u32 server_tick */
#define OG_S_COMMAND   0x83 /* char command[] ("vsync", "crash") */
#define OG_S_COLORS    0x84 /* u8 kind (OG_COLOR_*), u8 op (OG_COLOR_OP_*), u16 n,
                               n x { u8 r, u8 g, u8 b, u8 len, char text[len] } – names/items drawn in that colour */
#define OG_S_CHALLENGE 0x85 /* u32 challenge_id, u8 type (OG_CH_*), u8 nonce[16], u8 target, u32 a, u32 b */
#define OG_S_SIGS      0x86 /* u8 op (OG_SIGS_*), u16 n, n x { u16 id, u8 kind, u8 len, char pattern[len] } */

#define OG_POLICY_LEN    9
#define OG_CHALLENGE_LEN (1 + 4 + 1 + 16 + 1 + 4 + 4)
#define OG_RESPONSE_LEN  (1 + 4 + 1 + 1 + 32 + 4 + 4)

#define OG_SIGS_REPLACE 0
#define OG_SIGS_APPEND  1

#define OG_COLOR_NAME 1
#define OG_COLOR_ITEM 2
#define OG_COLOR_OP_REPLACE 0 /* the list replaces all entries of the kind */
#define OG_COLOR_OP_SET     1 /* add or change entries */
#define OG_COLOR_OP_REMOVE  2 /* remove entries (colour ignored) */

/* challenge types (OG_S_CHALLENGE) */
#define OG_CH_NONCE      1 /* digest = BLAKE2b-256(key = build secret, "OG/nonce" || nonce) */
#define OG_CH_CODE_RANGE 2 /* target 0 = game exe, 1 = guard dll; a = offset, b = length in the canonical code image;
                              digest = BLAKE2b-256(nonce || bytes) */
#define OG_CH_TIME       3 /* a = client tick (ms), b = client performance counter (ms); digest as OG_CH_NONCE */
#define OG_CH_FILE_RANGE 4 /* target = index into the protected file list of the profile; a = offset, b = length;
                              digest = BLAKE2b-256(nonce || bytes) */

#define OG_CH_ST_OK        0
#define OG_CH_ST_RANGE     1 /* offset/length outside the image or file */
#define OG_CH_ST_MISSING   2 /* file or module not present */
#define OG_CH_ST_UNKNOWN   3 /* challenge type not built into this client */

/* detection / signature kinds (OG_C_DETECT, OG_S_SIGS) */
#define OG_KIND_PROCESS      1
#define OG_KIND_WINDOW       2  /* window title contains */
#define OG_KIND_MODULE       3  /* loaded module name contains */
#define OG_KIND_INPUT        4  /* synthetic input blocked (report only) */
#define OG_KIND_GRF          5  /* resource override (report only) */
#define OG_KIND_INJECT       6  /* unknown module loaded (report only) */
#define OG_KIND_WINDOW_CLASS 7  /* exact window class name */
#define OG_KIND_FILE_NAME    8  /* file name in the client folder (case-insensitive, exact) */
#define OG_KIND_FILE_SHA256  9  /* hex sha256 of a file in the client folder or of a loaded module file */
#define OG_KIND_DRIVER       10 /* kernel driver / service name */
#define OG_KIND_GRF_SHA256   11 /* hex sha256 of a GRF listed in DATA.INI */
#define OG_KIND_API_HOOK     12 /* report only: API patched, text = function and owning module */
#define OG_KIND_GRF_MODIFIED 13 /* report only: GRF of the operator list differs (text = name) */
#define OG_KIND_GRF_UNKNOWN  14 /* report only: GRF in DATA.INI that is neither listed nor an allowed mod */
#define OG_KIND_GRF_MISSING  15 /* report only: required GRF of the operator list missing */
#define OG_KIND_MUTEX        16 /* named mutex / event / section exists (exact name, Local or Global) */
#define OG_KIND_REGISTRY     17 /* registry key exists: "HKCU\\path" or "HKLM\\path" */
/* GRF manifest of the operator (sent with OG_S_SIGS, id 0, never reported themselves):
 *   GRF_LIST "name|size|tail-sha256|full-sha256 or -|r or o"  accepted version of a GRF in DATA.INI (r = required);
 *            several entries with the same name = several accepted versions (patch rollouts)
 *   GRF_MOD  "tail-sha256|note"   allowed optional GRF under any name (skins, darkworld variants)
 *   OVERLAY  "data\\folder\\"    allowed loose-file folder (in addition to the built-in overlays)
 * tail-sha256 = SHA-256 of the 46-byte header followed by the bytes from the file table to the end of the file
 * (fast: every repack or entry change rewrites the table); full-sha256 = SHA-256 of the whole file, checked in
 * the background. */
#define OG_KIND_GRF_LIST     18
#define OG_KIND_GRF_MOD      19
#define OG_KIND_OVERLAY      20
#define OG_KIND_ALLOW_SHA256 64 /* allowlist: never report a file or module with this hash */
#define OG_KIND_ALLOW_PATH   65 /* allowlist: never report a module whose path contains this text */

#endif

```

`proto/og_wire.c`:

```c
/* OdinGuard Anti Cheat – see og_wire.h. Valid C99 and C++ (the server compiles it through og_wire.cpp). */
#include "og_wire.h"

#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>

int og_wire_client_hello(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_client_hello *h)
{
	uint16_t len;
	uint8_t nc;
	if (n < 4) return 0;
	if (og_rd16(p) != OG_HELLO_ID) return -1;
	len = og_rd16(p + 2);
	if (len < OG_CLIENT_HELLO_FIXED || len > OG_HELLO_MAX) return -1;
	if (n < len) return 0;
	nc = p[OG_CLIENT_HELLO_FIXED - 1];
	if (nc > OG_MAX_COMPONENTS || len != OG_CLIENT_HELLO_FIXED + (size_t)nc * (OG_COMPONENT_NAME + 32)) return -1;
	h->len = len;
	h->version = p[4];
	h->flags = p[5];
	h->eph_pub = p + 6;
	h->nonce = p + 38;
	h->unique_id = p + 70;
	h->exe_code = p + 102;
	h->build = p + 134;
	h->tag = p + 150;
	h->ncomp = nc;
	h->comp = p + OG_CLIENT_HELLO_FIXED;
	return len;
}

int og_wire_server_hello(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_server_hello *h)
{
	uint16_t len;
	if (n < 4) return 0;
	if (og_rd16(p) != OG_HELLO_ID) return -1;
	len = og_rd16(p + 2);
	if (len < OG_SERVER_HELLO_FIXED || len > OG_HELLO_MAX) return -1;
	if (n < len) return 0;
	h->len = len;
	h->version = p[4];
	h->status = p[5];
	h->eph_pub = p + 6;
	h->nonce = p + 38;
	h->sig = p + 70;
	h->message = p + OG_SERVER_HELLO_FIXED;
	h->message_len = (size_t)len - OG_SERVER_HELLO_FIXED;
	return len;
}

int og_wire_record(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, uint16_t *body_len)
{
	uint16_t b;
	if (n < 2) return 0;
	b = og_rd16(p);
	if (b == 0 || b > OG_RECORD_MAX + 1) return -1;
	if (n < (size_t)18 + b) return 0;
	*body_len = b;
	return 1;
}

int og_wire_policy(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_policy_msg *m)
{
	if (n < OG_POLICY_LEN || p[0] != OG_S_POLICY) return -1;
	m->block_vm = p[1];
	m->max_windows = p[2];
	m->alive_interval = og_rd16(p + 3);
	m->input_filter = p[5];
	m->grf_strict = p[6];
	return OG_POLICY_LEN;
}

int og_wire_alive(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_alive_msg *m)
{
	if (n < OG_ALIVE_LEN || p[0] != OG_C_ALIVE) return -1;
	m->seq = og_rd32(p + 1);
	m->exe_code = p + 5;
	m->unknown_modules = og_rd16(p + 37);
	m->flags = p[39];
	m->guard_code = p + 40;
	return OG_ALIVE_LEN;
}

int og_wire_challenge(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_challenge_msg *m)
{
	if (n < OG_CHALLENGE_LEN || p[0] != OG_S_CHALLENGE) return -1;
	m->id = og_rd32(p + 1);
	m->type = p[5];
	m->nonce = p + 6;
	m->target = p[22];
	m->a = og_rd32(p + 23);
	m->b = og_rd32(p + 27);
	return OG_CHALLENGE_LEN;
}

int og_wire_response(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_response_msg *m)
{
	if (n < OG_RESPONSE_LEN || p[0] != OG_C_RESPONSE) return -1;
	m->id = og_rd32(p + 1);
	m->type = p[5];
	m->status = p[6];
	m->digest = p + 7;
	m->a = og_rd32(p + 39);
	m->b = og_rd32(p + 43);
	return OG_RESPONSE_LEN;
}

int og_wire_sigs(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, uint8_t *op, og_sig_fn fn, void *ctx)
{
	size_t pos = 4;
	int cnt, i;
	if (n < 4 || p[0] != OG_S_SIGS) return -1;
	*op = p[1];
	cnt = og_rd16(p + 2);
	for (i = 0; i < cnt; i++) {
		uint8_t len;
		if (pos + 4 > n) return -1;
		len = p[pos + 3];
		if (pos + 4 + len > n) return -1;
		if (fn) fn(ctx, og_rd16(p + pos), p[pos + 2], (const char *)p + pos + 4, len);
		pos += 4 + (size_t)len;
	}
	return cnt;
}

int og_wire_colors(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, uint8_t *kind, uint8_t *op, og_color_fn fn, void *ctx)
{
	size_t pos = 5;
	int cnt, i;
	if (n < 5 || p[0] != OG_S_COLORS) return -1;
	*kind = p[1];
	*op = p[2];
	cnt = og_rd16(p + 3);
	for (i = 0; i < cnt; i++) {
		uint8_t len;
		if (pos + 4 > n) return -1;
		len = p[pos + 3];
		if (pos + 4 + len > n) return -1;
		if (fn) fn(ctx, ((uint32_t)p[pos] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[pos + 1] << 8) | p[pos + 2], (const char *)p + pos + 4, len);
		pos += 4 + (size_t)len;
	}
	return cnt;
}

size_t og_wire_write_challenge(uint8_t out[OG_CHALLENGE_LEN], const og_challenge_msg *m)
{
	out[0] = OG_S_CHALLENGE;
	og_wr32(out + 1, m->id);
	out[5] = m->type;
	memcpy(out + 6, m->nonce, 16);
	out[22] = m->target;
	og_wr32(out + 23, m->a);
	og_wr32(out + 27, m->b);
	return OG_CHALLENGE_LEN;
}

size_t og_wire_write_response(uint8_t out[OG_RESPONSE_LEN], const og_response_msg *m)
{
	out[0] = OG_C_RESPONSE;
	og_wr32(out + 1, m->id);
	out[5] = m->type;
	out[6] = m->status;
	if (m->digest) memcpy(out + 7, m->digest, 32);
	else memset(out + 7, 0, 32);
	og_wr32(out + 39, m->a);
	og_wr32(out + 43, m->b);
	return OG_RESPONSE_LEN;
}

/* ---------------- PE canonical image ---------------- */

#define PE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA 0x00000040u
#define PE_SCN_MEM_DISCARDABLE      0x02000000u
#define PE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE          0x20000000u
#define PE_SCN_MEM_WRITE            0x80000000u

int og_pe_section_included(uint32_t ch, int which)
{
	if (ch & (PE_SCN_MEM_WRITE | PE_SCN_MEM_DISCARDABLE)) return 0;
	if (ch & PE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE) return (which & OG_CANON_CODE) != 0;
	return (which & OG_CANON_RDATA) && (ch & PE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA);
}

typedef struct { uint32_t va, vsize, raw, rawsize, ch; } pe_sec;

static uint32_t rva_to_off(const pe_sec *s, int ns, uint32_t rva, size_t n)
{
	int i;
	for (i = 0; i < ns; i++)
		if (rva >= s[i].va && rva < s[i].va + s[i].rawsize && (size_t)s[i].raw + (rva - s[i].va) < n)
			return s[i].raw + (rva - s[i].va);
	return 0;
}

size_t og_pe_canonical(const uint8_t *f, size_t n, int which, uint8_t **out)
{
	uint32_t lfanew, opt, nsec, i, rel_rva, rel_size, iat_rva, iat_size, total = 0, pos = 0;
	uint16_t optsize;
	pe_sec s[96];
	uint8_t *img;
	*out = NULL;
	if (n < 0x40 || f[0] != 'M' || f[1] != 'Z') return 0;
	lfanew = og_rd32(f + 0x3c);
	if ((size_t)lfanew + 24 > n || memcmp(f + lfanew, "PE\0\0", 4) != 0) return 0;
	nsec = og_rd16(f + lfanew + 6);
	optsize = og_rd16(f + lfanew + 20);
	opt = lfanew + 24;
	if (nsec == 0 || nsec > 96 || (size_t)opt + optsize + nsec * 40u > n || optsize < 96 + 6 * 8) return 0;
	if (og_rd16(f + opt) != 0x10b) return 0; /* PE32 only (the 2018 client and the guard are 32-bit) */
	rel_rva = og_rd32(f + opt + 96 + 5 * 8);
	rel_size = og_rd32(f + opt + 96 + 5 * 8 + 4);
	/* the import address table is written by the loader even when its section is read-only */
	iat_rva = optsize >= 96 + 13 * 8 ? og_rd32(f + opt + 96 + 12 * 8) : 0;
	iat_size = optsize >= 96 + 13 * 8 ? og_rd32(f + opt + 96 + 12 * 8 + 4) : 0;
	for (i = 0; i < nsec; i++) {
		const uint8_t *h = f + opt + optsize + i * 40;
		s[i].vsize = og_rd32(h + 8);
		s[i].va = og_rd32(h + 12);
		s[i].rawsize = og_rd32(h + 16);
		s[i].raw = og_rd32(h + 20);
		s[i].ch = og_rd32(h + 36);
		if (!s[i].vsize) s[i].vsize = s[i].rawsize;
		if ((size_t)s[i].raw + s[i].rawsize > n) s[i].rawsize = s[i].raw < n ? (uint32_t)(n - s[i].raw) : 0;
		if (s[i].vsize > 64u * 1024 * 1024) return 0;
		if (og_pe_section_included(s[i].ch, which)) total += s[i].vsize;
	}
	if (!total || total > 256u * 1024 * 1024) return 0;
	img = (uint8_t *)calloc(1, total);
	if (!img) return 0;
	for (i = 0; i < nsec; i++) {
		uint32_t copy, start;
		if (!og_pe_section_included(s[i].ch, which)) continue;
		start = pos;
		copy = s[i].rawsize < s[i].vsize ? s[i].rawsize : s[i].vsize;
		if (copy) memcpy(img + pos, f + s[i].raw, copy);
		pos += s[i].vsize;
		if (iat_size && iat_rva < s[i].va + s[i].vsize && iat_rva + iat_size > s[i].va) {
			uint32_t a = iat_rva > s[i].va ? iat_rva : s[i].va;
			uint32_t b = iat_rva + iat_size < s[i].va + s[i].vsize ? iat_rva + iat_size : s[i].va + s[i].vsize;
			memset(img + start + (a - s[i].va), 0, b - a);
		}
		/* zero every HIGHLOW slot inside this section */
		if (rel_rva && rel_size) {
			uint32_t r = rva_to_off(s, (int)nsec, rel_rva, n), end;
			if (r) {
				end = r + rel_size;
				if (end > n) end = (uint32_t)n;
				while (r + 8 <= end) {
					uint32_t page = og_rd32(f + r), bsize = og_rd32(f + r + 4), k;
					if (bsize < 8 || r + bsize > end) break;
					for (k = 8; k + 2 <= bsize; k += 2) {
						uint16_t e = og_rd16(f + r + k);
						uint32_t rva = page + (e & 0xFFF);
						if ((e >> 12) == 3 && rva >= s[i].va && rva + 4 <= s[i].va + s[i].vsize)
							memset(img + start + (rva - s[i].va), 0, 4);
					}
					r += bsize;
				}
			}
		}
	}
	*out = img;
	return total;
}

```

`proto/og_wire.h`:

```h
/* OdinGuard Anti Cheat – pure parsers and writers for the wire protocol (og_proto.h) and a portable PE
 * canonicaliser. No OS calls, no allocation except og_pe_canonical. Used by the client DLL, the server module
 * (compiled as C++ through og_wire.cpp) and the native fuzz test (tests/fuzz_wire.c).
 *
 * Return convention of the parsers: > 0 = number of bytes the message uses, 0 = incomplete (stream framing
 * only), -1 = malformed (drop the connection or the message). */
#ifndef OG_WIRE_H
#define OG_WIRE_H

#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>

#include "og_proto.h"

#ifdef __cplusplus
extern "C" {
#endif

static inline uint16_t og_rd16(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint16_t)(p[0] | (p[1] << 8)); }
static inline uint32_t og_rd32(const uint8_t *p) { return (uint32_t)p[0] | ((uint32_t)p[1] << 8) | ((uint32_t)p[2] << 16) | ((uint32_t)p[3] << 24); }
static inline void og_wr16(uint8_t *p, uint16_t v) { p[0] = (uint8_t)v; p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); }
static inline void og_wr32(uint8_t *p, uint32_t v) { p[0] = (uint8_t)v; p[1] = (uint8_t)(v >> 8); p[2] = (uint8_t)(v >> 16); p[3] = (uint8_t)(v >> 24); }

typedef struct {
	uint16_t len;
	uint8_t version, flags, ncomp;
	const uint8_t *eph_pub, *nonce, *unique_id, *exe_code, *build, *tag, *comp; /* comp: ncomp x (16 + 32) */
} og_client_hello;

typedef struct {
	uint16_t len;
	uint8_t version, status;
	const uint8_t *eph_pub, *nonce, *sig, *message;
	size_t message_len;
} og_server_hello;

typedef struct { uint8_t block_vm, max_windows, input_filter, grf_strict; uint16_t alive_interval; } og_policy_msg;
typedef struct { uint32_t seq; const uint8_t *exe_code; uint16_t unknown_modules; uint8_t flags; const uint8_t *guard_code; } og_alive_msg;
typedef struct { uint32_t id; uint8_t type; const uint8_t *nonce; uint8_t target; uint32_t a, b; } og_challenge_msg;
typedef struct { uint32_t id; uint8_t type, status; const uint8_t *digest; uint32_t a, b; } og_response_msg;

typedef void (*og_sig_fn)(void *ctx, uint16_t id, uint8_t kind, const char *pattern, size_t len);
typedef void (*og_color_fn)(void *ctx, uint32_t rgb, const char *text, size_t len);

int og_wire_client_hello(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_client_hello *h);
int og_wire_server_hello(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_server_hello *h);
/* record framing: 1 = a complete record of 18 + *body_len bytes is at p */
int og_wire_record(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, uint16_t *body_len);

/* control messages (p[0] is the message type) */
int og_wire_policy(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_policy_msg *m);
int og_wire_alive(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_alive_msg *m);
int og_wire_challenge(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_challenge_msg *m);
int og_wire_response(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, og_response_msg *m);
/* returns the number of entries delivered, -1 if malformed (entries before the error were delivered) */
int og_wire_sigs(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, uint8_t *op, og_sig_fn fn, void *ctx);
int og_wire_colors(const uint8_t *p, size_t n, uint8_t *kind, uint8_t *op, og_color_fn fn, void *ctx);

size_t og_wire_write_challenge(uint8_t out[OG_CHALLENGE_LEN], const og_challenge_msg *m);
size_t og_wire_write_response(uint8_t out[OG_RESPONSE_LEN], const og_response_msg *m);

/* Canonical image of a PE file (32-bit): the sections a guard hashes, in section order, each as large as in
 * memory (zero padded), with every HIGHLOW relocation slot and the import address table zeroed, so it does not depend on the load address.
 * OG_CANON_CODE: executable, non-writable sections. OG_CANON_RDATA: also read-only initialized data
 * (not discardable). Returns the size and sets *out (malloc'd, caller frees), 0 if the file is not a usable PE. */
#define OG_CANON_CODE  1
#define OG_CANON_RDATA 2
size_t og_pe_canonical(const uint8_t *file, size_t n, int which, uint8_t **out);
/* section filter shared by the file and the in-memory variant */
int og_pe_section_included(uint32_t characteristics, int which);

#ifdef __cplusplus
}
#endif

#endif

```

`server/README.md`:

```md
# OdinGuard Anti Cheat – server module (rAthena)

Release copy of the server module (working copy: an rAthena fork; refreshed with `tools/sync_server.sh`, which also
writes `HOOKS.txt` with every hook line). Step-by-step integration: [../docs/INTEGRATION.md](../docs/INTEGRATION.md).
A Studio release (`og build`) contains this folder plus the generated config.

## Files

| File | Goes to | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `src/common/odinguard.cpp/.hpp` | `src/common/` | socket layer: handshake (X25519, pinned Ed25519 key, profile tag), XChaCha20-Poly1305 records with key rotation, config, policy, signature package and GRF manifest, alive check, challenges, SQL tables |
| `src/common/og_wire.c/.h`, `og_wire.cpp`, `og_proto.h` | `src/common/` | wire protocol and parsers, byte-identical with the client (`proto/`) |
| `src/common/og_crypto.cpp` | `src/common/` | compiles `3rdparty/monocypher/monocypher.c` |
| `src/login/og_login.cpp/.hpp` | `src/login/` | login check: client report, machine bans (exact + fuzzy), `og_client`/`og_component` |
| `src/map/og_map.cpp/.hpp` | `src/map/` | events, kicks, bans, `!ping`/`!vsync`/`!crash`, machine limit, lite ground skills, name and item colours |
| `src/map/og_map_guard.cpp` | `src/map/` | flags and ban waves, rate limit, behaviour rules (no-delay, autopot, macro), honeypot, captcha, command registry |
| `conf/odinguard_athena.conf` | `conf/` | every switch with defaults; the Studio writes `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt` |
| `sql/odinguard.sql` | – | reference DDL; the servers create the tables at start |

Auras were part of OdinGuard up to 1.0 previews; they are a separate rAthena feature now (not part of this repository).

## Hooks (exact lines: `HOOKS.txt`)

| Where | What |
|---|---|
| `src/common/Makefile.in`, `CMakeLists.txt` | `odinguard.o og_crypto.o og_wire.o`; `og_proto.h og_wire.h og_wire.c` in the common headers (otherwise make does not rebuild `og_wire.o`) |
| `socket.hpp` `struct socket_data` | `void* og;` connection state |
| `socket.cpp` `recv_to_fifo` / `send_from_fifo` | `og_handles_recv/og_recv`, `og_handles_send/og_send`: decrypt/encrypt OdinGuard connections, plain ones pass |
| `socket.cpp` `session_has_output` | `og_has_pending` |
| `socket.cpp` `make_connection` | `og_mark_plain`: inter-server links are never OdinGuard connections |
| `socket.cpp` `delete_session` / `socket_init` / `socket_final` | `og_session_free`, `og_init`, `og_final` |
| `login.cpp` / `loginclif.cpp` | `og_login_init/final`; `og_login_check` in `logclif_auth_ok` (banned machine code 4, missing guard when required, old version) |
| `char_clif.cpp` `chclif_parse_reqtoconnect`, `clif.cpp` `clif_parse_WantToConnection` | refuse clients without the guard when `og_required` |
| `clif.cpp` `clif_parse_LoadEndAck` | `og_map_on_load` (colour lists), `og_map_honeypot_spawn` |
| `clif.cpp` `clif_parse_GlobalMessage` | `og_map_chat_command` (`!` commands) |
| `clif.cpp` packet dispatch | `og_map_packet` (rate limit) |
| `clif.cpp` skill/item/attack handlers | `og_map_skill_refused`, `og_map_skill_used`, `og_map_item_used`, `og_map_hp_update`, `og_map_honeypot_hit` |
| `clif.cpp` `clif_getareachar_skillunit`, `clif_skill_poseffect` | lite ground skills per viewer |
| `map.cpp` | `og_map_init`, `og_map_on_quit` |
| `pc.cpp` `pc_authok` | `og_map_machine_limit` |
| `atcommand.cpp` | `@ogban @ogunban @oginfo @ogflags @ogbanwave @namecolor @lgp @square @circle @aoes` + `ACMD_DEF`s |
| `conf/groups.yml` | player group: `lgp`, `square`, `circle`, `aoes` |

## Config keys (generated by the Studio)

Modules: `og_enable`, `og_required`, `og_log_only`, `og_rate_limit`, `og_hwid`, `og_multi_client`, `og_heartbeat`,
`og_integrity`, `og_signatures`, `og_grf_rules`, `og_input_filter`, `og_client_commands`, `og_colors`,
`og_lgp_enable`, `og_ban_system`, `og_behaviour`, `og_ch_<nonce|code|time|file|captcha|honeypot>`,
`og_competitive_pack`. References: `og_guard_file`, `og_protected_file`, `og_sigpack`, `og_sigpack_key`,
`og_sigpack_min_version`, `og_allowed_exe`. GRF manifest: `og_grf_file`, `og_grf_mod`, `og_grf_overlay`,
`og_grf_<modified|unknown|missing>_action`. Commands: `og_cmd_<id>`, `og_cmdgroup_<id>`, `og_cmdrate_<id>`,
`og_cmdname_<id>`. Secrets (environment preferred): `ODINGUARD_KEY`/`og_key`, `ODINGUARD_PROTO_SALT`/`og_proto_salt`,
`ODINGUARD_BUILD_SECRET`/`og_build_secret`.

## Tables

`og_client` (machine ↔ account, build, exe hash), `og_component` (salted hardware components), `og_ban` (machine
bans), `og_event` (every detection and action), `og_flag` (flags with score for the ban waves).

`server/conf/odinguard_athena.conf`:

```conf
// OdinGuard Anti Cheat settings. Local overrides: conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt (created at the first start).
// The OdinGuard Studio generates the profile values (key, proto salt, build secret, signature package, module
// switches, commands, auras) into conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt; the environment variables ODINGUARD_KEY,
// ODINGUARD_PROTO_SALT and ODINGUARD_BUILD_SECRET override them (keep them out of git).

// Turn the protocol on. Clients with OdinGuard then talk encrypted; clients without it still work
// unless og_required is on.
og_enable: no

// Refuse logins (and char/map connections) of clients without OdinGuard.
og_required: no

// Only write events (console + og_event table) instead of kicking/banning. Use it for the first days.
og_log_only: yes

// Ed25519 seed of the server, 64 hex characters (tools/og_keygen.py in the OdinGuard repo).
// Keep it secret; the matching public key is compiled into odinguard.dll.
//og_key:

// Oldest accepted client protocol version (2 = OdinGuard Anti Cheat 1.x; lower values are raised to 2).
og_min_version: 2

// Profile values of the client build (Studio): protocol salt (32 hex) and build secret (64 hex). A client built
// for another profile is refused with a message. Empty salt = the development profile.
//og_proto_salt:
//og_build_secret:

// Heartbeat: the client reports every og_alive_interval seconds, missing reports for
// og_alive_timeout seconds disconnect the player.
og_alive_interval: 30
og_alive_timeout: 120

// Client side: maximum game windows per computer (0 = unlimited) and refuse virtual machines.
og_max_windows: 0
og_block_vm: no
og_vm_action: kick

// Server side: maximum characters online from one machine (hardware id; 0 = unlimited, GMs not counted).
og_max_per_machine: 0

// A login is refused when at least this many identifying hardware parts (machine guid, volume serial,
// disk serial, mac, smbios uuid) are equal to those of a banned machine. The new id is banned too.
og_ban_match: 2

// Block synthetic mouse/keyboard input (macros, auto-pot tools) in the game window.
og_input_filter: no

// Report resource overrides (loose files in data\ or unknown GRFs that replace protected files).
og_grf_strict: no

// Actions: log, kick, ban (machine ban + kick), flag (score in og_flag, player stays) or flagban (flag now, ban
// with the next ban wave, so a cheater cannot tell which check fired).
og_integrity_action: kick
og_tamper_action: kick
og_grf_action: kick
og_inject_action: log

// Allowed in-memory code hashes of the game exe (from the client report, odinguard.log "exe_code").
// Empty = every exe is accepted. One line per allowed build.
//og_allowed_exe: <64 hex characters>

// Known cheat and automation tools: kind (process, window or module), action, pattern.
// The pattern is matched case-insensitively as part of the process file name, the window title
// or the module file name. The list is sent to the client at login, so it can be changed
// without a client update.
og_signature: process,kick,openkore
og_signature: window,kick,OpenKore
og_signature: process,kick,wpepro
og_signature: window,kick,WPE PRO
og_signature: module,kick,wpespy
og_signature: process,kick,rpe.exe

`server/patches/README.md`:

```md
# OdinGuard Anti Cheat – patch for upstream rAthena

`rathena-4cd08b7.patch` installs the complete server module into upstream rAthena
([rathena/rathena](https://github.com/rathena/rathena), branch `master`).

| | |
|---|---|
| Base commit | `4cd08b739035721b2cbffa0310dbbf0eac081d9d` (2026-11-23, "Removed duplicate header includes in clif.cpp and npc.cpp (#10186)") |
| Content | 37 files, +6717 / −6 lines: module files, Monocypher, all hooks, build files, config |

## What the patch contains

- Module files (unchanged copies of `server/src` and `server/conf`): `src/common/odinguard.cpp/.hpp`, `og_crypto.cpp`,
  `og_proto.h`, `og_wire.c/.h/.cpp`; `src/login/og_login.cpp/.hpp`; `src/map/og_map.cpp/.hpp`, `og_map_guard.cpp`;
  `conf/odinguard_athena.conf`.
- `3rdparty/monocypher/` (`monocypher.c/.h`, `LICENCE.md`) – upstream rAthena does not ship Monocypher.
- Hooks (see `../HOOKS.txt` and `../README.md`): `socket.cpp/.hpp`, `login.cpp`, `loginclif.cpp`, `char_clif.cpp`,
  `clif.cpp/.hpp`, `map.cpp`, `pc.cpp`, `atcommand.cpp` (`@ogban @ogunban @oginfo @ogflags @ogbanwave @namecolor
  @lgp @square @circle @aoes`), `conf/groups.yml` (player group: `lgp`, `square`, `circle`, `aoes`).
- Build files: `src/common/Makefile.in` (`odinguard.o og_crypto.o og_wire.o`; `og_proto.h og_wire.h og_wire.c` as
  header dependencies so `og_wire.o` is rebuilt), `src/common/CMakeLists.txt`, and the Visual Studio projects and
  filters of common, login-server, map-server and map-server-generator (`og_wire.c` is listed as a header because
  `og_wire.cpp` includes it). Login and map `Makefile.in`/`CMakeLists.txt` pick up the new `.cpp` files by wildcard.

Not part of the patch: the unrelated custom changes of the development fork (auras, `@whosell`, battleground
extensions, `max_clients_per_ip`).

## Apply

Plain `git apply` (no `git am`, the file is a diff, not a mail series):

```sh
cd rathena
git checkout 4cd08b739035721b2cbffa0310dbbf0eac081d9d   # or a newer master, see below
git apply --check /path/to/OdinGuard/server/patches/rathena-4cd08b7.patch
git apply /path/to/OdinGuard/server/patches/rathena-4cd08b7.patch
./configure --enable-packetver=20180620     # your PACKETVER
make clean && make server
```

Without git: `patch -p1 < rathena-4cd08b7.patch`.

Then continue with [docs/INTEGRATION.md](../../docs/INTEGRATION.md) section 6, steps 5–6 (secrets, first start). The
servers create `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt` and the tables `og_client`, `og_component`, `og_ban`, `og_event`,
`og_flag` on the first start.

## Newer rAthena: resolving conflicts

The module files never conflict (they are new). Conflicts can only appear in the hook context:

1. Try a three-way apply first: `git apply --3way rathena-4cd08b7.patch` (needs the base commit in your history,
   i.e. a clone of upstream rather than a tarball). Or apply with rejects: `git apply --reject ...` and fix the
   `*.rej` hunks by hand.
2. For every rejected hunk look up the hook in `../HOOKS.txt` (file:line:content of the reference fork) and the
   function it belongs to in `../README.md` ("Hooks" table). Place the line in the same function at the same logical
   spot; the line numbers in HOOKS.txt are only a guide.
3. `clif_og_honeypot()` (listed in HOOKS.txt) goes into `src/map/clif.cpp` after `clif_sendfakenpc`; its declaration
   in `src/map/clif.hpp` must be outside any `#ifdef` (used by `og_map_guard.cpp`).
4. Typical upstream drift: renamed/reshaped packet structs in `clif.cpp` (`packet_idle_unit`,
   `PACKET_ZC_NOTIFY_GROUNDSKILL`), `map_session_data*` vs `map_session_data&` parameters, and new `ACMD_DEF` list
   order. The hooks only need `sd`, `fd`, `skill_id`, `target_id` and the packet buffer.
5. Rebuild and check the map-server log for `OdinGuard Anti Cheat: enabled`.

## Smoke test (base 4cd08b7)

- `make server -j3` in `alpine:3.23` (`./configure --enable-packetver=20180620`): login, char and map server built
  without errors; the only new warning is `-Wshadow` inside `monocypher.c`.
  Rebuilt with `make server -j2` after the module update (`BCryptGenRandom` on Windows): no errors; the Linux
  startup path is unchanged, so the run below was not repeated.
- CMake (`cmake -DPACKETVER=20180620`, targets `login-server char-server map-server`) on the same tree: built.
- Run: MariaDB 11 in its own Docker network, `sql-files/main.sql` + `logs.sql` imported, `conf/import/odinguard_conf.txt`
  with `og_enable: yes`, `og_log_only: yes` and random `og_key`/`og_proto_salt`/`og_build_secret`:
  - login, char and map server log `OdinGuard Anti Cheat: enabled (required: no, log only: yes, 22 signatures,
    challenges)`;
  - char-server connected to the login-server, map-server connected to the char-server, `Map Server is now online`
    (inter-server links stay plain);
  - the tables `og_ban`, `og_client`, `og_component`, `og_event`, `og_flag` were created;
  - a plain client login packet (0x0064, unknown account) was answered with `0x083e` (refused, code 0), i.e. clients
    without OdinGuard still pass when `og_required` is off.
- Not covered here: a real OdinGuard client handshake (use the project's end-to-end test suite for that).

## PACKETVER notes

- Tested with `PACKETVER 20180620`; upstream's default is `20211103`. The module itself has no PACKETVER switches.
- Lite ground skills (`@lgp`, `@square`, `@circle`, `@aoes`) replace units only in the skill unit packet `0x09ca`,
  i.e. `PACKETVER >= 20130731`. The `clif_skill_poseffect` hook hides the heavy animation for those players with every
  PACKETVER, so with older PACKETVER they would see neither animation nor cells: keep `og_lgp_enable` off there.
- The honeypot unit (`clif_og_honeypot`) uses `packet_idle_unit` with the same PACKETVER conditions as
  `clif_sendfakenpc`.

## Known limitations

- Windows: the Visual Studio project entries are included but untested (`odinguard.cpp` uses `BCryptGenRandom` there
  and links `bcrypt.lib` via `#pragma comment`; Linux uses `/dev/urandom`).

+#ifdef MONOCYPHER_CPP_NAMESPACE

+/////////////////
+/// Utilities ///
+/////////////////
+#define FOR_T(type, i, start, end) for (type i = (start); i < (end); i++)
+#define FOR(i, start, end)         FOR_T(size_t, i, start, end)
+#define COPY(dst, src, size)       FOR(_i_, 0, size) (dst)[_i_] = (src)[_i_]
+#define ZERO(buf, size)            FOR(_i_, 0, size) (buf)[_i_] = 0
+#define WIPE_CTX(ctx)              crypto_wipe(ctx   , sizeof(*(ctx)))
+#define WIPE_BUFFER(buffer)        crypto_wipe(buffer, sizeof(buffer))
+#define MIN(a, b)                  ((a) <= (b) ? (a) : (b))
+#define MAX(a, b)                  ((a) >= (b) ? (a) : (b))
